  3. Type the six-character code shown in the dialog. The red Stop everything button stays disabled until the code matches — a slip of the mouse is never enough.
  4. Press Stop everything. The stop runs immediately; a notification lists what was cancelled and paused. If some running work could not be cancelled at once, the notification reads Emergency stop partly applied: the assignments are paused, AI is off for a platform-wide stop, and the follow-up passes cancel what they reach.
  5. The dialog then asks why. The stop never waits for this: it is already done. Type the reason and Save reason, or Skip. The reason is written in the audit trail next to the stop and on every assignment the stop paused.

The stop is instant, the explanation comes after

An emergency does not wait for a form. That is why the reason is asked right after the stop, not before it.

docs.title: What you see afterwards
docs.text:
• A red banner on every page — Emergency stop in effect, with how many assignments are paused, whether AI is off, who pressed it, when and why. It carries a Resume button for whoever may lift the stop. A platform-wide stop shows the banner to every user, whether or not it paused any of their assignments; only an administrator can lift it, so regular users see the fact without a button.
  • Assignments show a red Emergency stop badge instead of Paused, in the assignment page, the agent's assignment list and the status tile. The assignment page explains who pressed the stop, when and why.
  • Runs cancelled by the stop carry the cause Stopped by an emergency stop. on their card and detail page.
  • Chat, with the whole platform stopped, shows AI as switched off.
  • Logs hold one entry per stop and per resume with the counts and the reason, plus one pause / resume entry per assignment.

While the stop is in effect, an assignment it paused cannot be re-enabled with its ordinary on/off switch, and an agent cannot re-enable it through its tools. The only way back is to lift the stop.

docs.title: Lift the emergency stop
docs.text:
Press Resume in the banner, or open your profile menu and choose Resume my activity or, as an administrator, Resume the whole platform.

You are asked why. The reason is mandatory and is recorded on the resume entry and on every assignment that is re-enabled.

Lifting the stop:

  • re-enables only the assignments the stop paused — an assignment someone paused by hand stays paused
  • while a platform-wide stop is in effect, only lifting that stop resumes anything: a user cannot resume their own activity underneath it
  • lifting the platform-wide stop leaves in place a stop a user pressed for their own activity: that user lifts it themselves
  • an assignment in two people's activity (one owns it, it runs as the other) stays paused while either of their stops is in effect: it comes back once both have lifted theirs, whichever paused it
  • for the whole platform, sets the AI switch back to what it was before the stop — on, off, or Deployment default — so an administrator who had AI off keeps it off, and a platform started without AI stays without AI (see Running without AI); a change made in Settings while the stop was in effect is kept
  • does not resurrect cancelled work

docs.title: Prepare for an emergency without a session
docs.text:
Nobody may be signed in when the stop is needed: the on-call engineer has only a terminal, or a monitoring system must press the button itself. For that, an administrator creates the emergency stop API token in Settings → Security → Emergency stop.

  • Generate token creates it. It is shown once; only a hash is stored, so it can never be displayed again.
  • Print the procedure opens a page for paper or PDF: what the stop does, when to use it, the exact command with the token, how to lift the stop afterwards, and a space for the people to call. Keep it with the on-call material. The page is produced in the language of your interface.
  • Rotate token invalidates the current token and issues a new one. Every printed procedure carrying the old token becomes invalid and must be reprinted.
  • Revoke disables the API path until a new token is generated. The button in the profile menu keeps working.

The section shows the token's prefix, who generated it and when, and when it was last used.

Treat the printed page like a physical key

Anyone holding the token can stop the whole platform. It does nothing else — it cannot read or change anything — but rotate it as soon as a printed copy is lost or exposed. Every refused attempt to use it is recorded in the logs under the token owner's name.

Pressing the stop with the token always covers the whole platform and is attributed to the administrator who generated the token. The command and the responses are described in Emergency stop API.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Read Emergency stop API to press the stop from a script or a monitoring hook, or Running without AI for what a platform with AI switched off can still do.

docs.title: Platform Health
docs.text:
Platform Health (formerly the Concierge) is a company-managed fleet of agents that looks after the platform's other agents and flows. It consolidates memories, diagnoses agents and flows from their traces, ratings and run history, tries changes on sandbox copies, measures them with evaluations, and files improvement proposals that the people who manage the target approve. Nothing it proposes reaches production without that approval, and an applied change that regresses is rolled back.

Built in

Platform Health is built in: no feature flag is needed. An administrator turns it on in Settings > Automations > Platform Health. The former /concierge page and /api/v1/concierge routes still answer for one minor release: the page redirects to /health, the API routes are deprecated aliases of /api/v1/health and carry a Deprecation header.

docs.title: The fleet
docs.text:
The platform ships a built-in fleet named Platform Health, in a company-managed workspace of the same name, with five agents:

Agent Role Platform Health The orchestrator. Investigates a target after a signal or a request by handing the work to the specialists, writes the weekly digest, and answers administrators in chat. Memory Steward Consolidates the memory of agents whose managers opted in. Quality Analyst Diagnoses agents and drafts persona, skill and assignment-prompt variants. Flow Lab Diagnoses flows and drafts repairs, optimizations and new flows on sandbox copies. Experimenter Measures variants with evaluations and files the proposals.

The fleet, its agents, their assignments and its workspace are built in and read-only for everyone, administrators included: nobody edits, switches off, deletes, duplicates or forks them, and every attempt answers "Platform Health is built in and read-only." The platform rewrites their definition at every start. What an administrator tunes is set in Settings > Automations > Platform Health (below). None of the agents can edit an agent or a flow directly. The fleet never supervises itself.

The fleet's tools and skills are its own. The Tools page and the agent builder show one health group, Platform Health (read signals, cycles and digests; ask it to improve an agent or a flow); the specialists' tools are one internal group that only the fleet's agents carry. The Skills catalogue shows Platform Health: module checks (the OpenCTI, OpenAEV and OpenCRQ checks, one section per module), Fleet health advisory and Fleet design and operations; the Memory Steward, Quality Analyst, Flow Lab and Experimenter skills are internal, bound to their agents only.

Every piece of Platform Health work is a run of one of the fleet's assignments, and every run starts inside a cycle: a unit of work with its own share of the Platform Health budget. Each cycle ends with a digest.

docs.title: Settings > Automations > Platform Health
docs.text:
The settings are one section. A bar at its top (On this page) jumps to its four groups, each with a link that can be shared (#health-settings-status, #health-settings-spend, #health-settings-checks, #health-settings-alerts), then to the companion pets:

Group Blocks Status and scope Status (enable, name), scope Spend limits Budget, analysis, Module Analyst (XTM One modes) Health checks Schedule, signals, module thresholds, durations, dry-run Alerts Alert emails Block What it sets Enable, name, scope, budget Whether Platform Health works, the name the entry points and refusals use, which agents and flows it supervises among those their managers enrolled (all of them, or a list), and its budget per cycle and per month, in tokens and in dollars. Analysis Whether the routing model explains the findings, and its hard ceilings per day and per month, in tokens and in dollars (see Analysis). Schedule When each fleet-wide cycle starts, as a cron expression in the time zone chosen: memory consolidation (default every night at 02:00), quality review (Mondays 03:00), flow review (Mondays 04:00) and the weekly digest (Mondays 07:00). Each can be switched off. A schedule never fires at start-up: it first fires at its next occurrence. Signals The thresholds below, each with its own switch. Alert emails Off by default. On, Platform Health emails the recipients named (up to 20) from the platform sender: one email per critical finding as soon as a health pass opens it, once per finding, and one digest a day (UTC) of the open findings at or above the minimum severity, sent only when there is at least one. Each of the two can be switched off. Nothing is sent while the platform email (SMTP) is not configured; no model call. Durations How long an applied proposal is watched for a regression (7 days), how long a flow that replaces an assignment runs in shadow first (3 days), how long it is watched after the switch (7 days), and how many shadow runs it needs (5). Dry-run Every write of every Platform Health agent is logged instead of executed: memory changes, proposals, sandbox copies. Digests count what was logged.

docs.title: Spend limits locked by default
docs.text:
Platform Health spends outside the agentic quota: its own ceilings are the only bound on that spend. They are therefore locked by default. In the Spend limits group, the ceilings of the Budget, Analysis and Module Analyst blocks show their built-in defaults, read-only, with a lock and the variable that unlocks them; a change to one of them is refused. A value stored before the lock is kept, not applied.

To change them, set PLATFORM_HEALTH_SPEND_LIMITS_UNLOCKED=true in the platform's environment and restart: the stored values apply again and the ceilings are editable. The switches of the analysis and of the Module Analyst stay editable either way, since turning them off only lowers the spend. GET /api/v1/health/settings/spend-limits reports the lock and, for each ceiling, the value in force, its default, the stored value and its source (default or database).

docs.title: Name
docs.text:
The Name field sets the name the entry points ("Improve with …") and the refusals use. The page, the navigation entry, the Settings section, the orchestrator agent, its fleet and its workspace always read Platform Health: the fleet is built in, so the platform writes that name on them at every start, over a former Concierge name too. Left empty, the name is Platform Health. It is 1 to 40 characters, without line breaks or control characters; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.

Saving a new name renames no agent, fleet or workspace, and the agents' personas are not changed: the name is what people read, not an instruction to the model.

A schedule that is due while the budget is reached, or while agentic AI is off, starts nothing: its last firing and the reason are shown under the schedule, and it tries again at its next occurrence.

docs.title: Companion pets
docs.text:
The Companion pets block lists the pets users may pick for their companion (see Platform Health). Butler is built in and cannot be removed. Add a pet takes a pet in the Codex pet format, as one .zip holding pet.json and its spritesheet, or as the two files:

  • pet.json with id (lowercase letters, digits and dashes), displayName, an optional description, spritesheetPath (a .webp or .png path inside the package) and, for a version 2 pet, "spriteVersionNumber": 2;
  • a spritesheet of 8 columns of 192x208 cells: 1536x1872 for version 1 (9 rows: idle, running right, running left, waving, jumping, failed, waiting, running, review), 1536x2288 for version 2 (two more rows, the look directions).

A package of more than 8 MB, an SVG or any image that is not a single-frame PNG or WebP of the exact size, a path that leaves the package, or a field out of bounds is refused with the rule it broke. The platform keeps its own re-encoding of the spritesheet, never the uploaded file. Removing a pet shows the default pet to the users who had picked it.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
Signals are read by the scheduler without any model call, only for the agents and flows of the supervision scope, from figures the platform already keeps (no conversation content):

Signal Default threshold Read Feedback drop An agent's weighted feedback score is 10 points lower over the last 3 days than over the 3 days before, with at least 10 ratings in the last 3 days Every 15 minutes Failure spike More than 5 % of the last 20 finished runs of an assignment or a flow failed Every 15 minutes, for the assignments and flows that ran since Cost drift An agent's cost per assignment run is 20 % higher over the last 7 days than over the 7 days before, with at least 10 runs in each period Hourly, from the daily usage figures Model change The model a supervised agent resolves to changes Hourly

A signal starts one investigation on its target when it crosses its threshold. It does not start another while it stays crossed; it is ready again once the figure is back under the threshold. While an investigation, or any other cycle, is open on a target, nothing starts a second one there: the request or the signal is recorded and refused.

docs.title: Platform checks
docs.text:
In XTM One mode, AI switched off included, the health pass also checks the XTM One platform itself every 5 minutes. These checks read a setting or one record, call no model and need no enrolment; in Copilot mode they record nothing.

Check Severity Fails when Registration token Critical PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOKEN is the published default value, which authenticates nobody Licence Critical A Filigran licence is installed and refused (no licence installed is Community Edition, not a finding) Licence expiry Warning The validated Filigran licence expires within 30 days Email (SMTP) Info No SMTP host is configured, so the platform sends no email (nor can agents, through the Platform email integration) XTM Hub registration Info The platform is not registered with XTM Hub, or its registration lost connectivity or must be done again Integration broken Warning A company-managed integration is in error, must be re-authorized, or failed its last connection test (one finding per integration) MCP server broken Warning An enabled company-managed MCP server could not renew its OAuth token (one finding per server) Knowledge base indexing stalled Warning A knowledge base has documents still processing after 1 hour (one finding per knowledge base) Stale embeddings Warning A knowledge base was embedded with another model than the platform's embedding model (one finding per knowledge base) Default model Critical No default model is set, so agents without a model of their own cannot run Embedding model Critical No embedding model is set, so knowledge bases can neither index nor search Quota near ceiling Warning A platform-wide agentic ceiling is 90 % used in its current period (one finding per period). Reading it consumes no quota Dependency unreachable Critical Redis or the object storage does not answer its readiness probe within 4 seconds (one finding per dependency) Trace backlog Warning Over 1,000 traces wait to be written to the trace store, so analytics and traces lag No worker running Critical No worker says it is running, so queued runs, renders and indexing wait until one starts Model failing Warning Over 5 % of a model's calls in the last hour failed, with at least 20 calls (one finding per model) Version behind Info, Warning A newer XTM One release is published (info), or two or more (warning). Read once a day from the public release list; an air-gapped platform records nothing Certificate expiry Warning The TLS certificate of the public URL (FRONTEND_URL) expires within 21 days or is refused (expired, untrusted, another host name). Read once a day; a URL the backend cannot reach records nothing

A finding resolves by itself after two passes in a row without its cause; fixing or deleting the integration, server or knowledge base it names resolves it too.

docs.title: Run checks as
docs.text:
The agentic checks of OpenCTI, OpenAEV and OpenCRQ read each module through its integration, as one user: the Run checks as user. The XTM One administrator often has no access to the modules, so an administrator picks a user who has, in Settings > Agents and automations > Platform Health > Health checks > Run checks as, or on the Modules step of the guided Set up the CTEM loop setup. The user must reach every registered module's integration (granted to them and connected for them): otherwise the save is refused and the message names the modules the user cannot read.

There is no other identity: while no user is set, or when the user loses access to a module, no agentic check of that module runs and its card on the Platform Health page reads Checks need a run-as user with access, with a link to the setting. Set the user, then Run checks now: the card shows the checks passed, warned and failed.

docs.title: OpenCTI checks
docs.text:
In XTM One mode, AI switched off included, every registered OpenCTI is checked every 5 minutes, with no enrolment. The heartbeat check reads the registration; the others read the health snapshot OpenCTI sends with its registration, as long as it is under 15 minutes old. An OpenCTI release that sends no snapshot is only checked for its heartbeat. Nothing is stored while PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOKEN is the published default value.

Check Severity Fails when Heartbeat Critical OpenCTI has not registered for 15 minutes Connector silent Warning An active connector has not reported for 30 minutes (one finding per connector) (E) Connector errors Warning A connector has over 10 works in error (one finding per connector) (E) Queue depth Warning Over 100,000 messages wait in the broker (E) No queue consumer Critical Messages wait in the broker and no worker reads them Search engine Warning, Critical The Elasticsearch or OpenSearch cluster is yellow (warning) or red (critical) Search engine disk Warning The search engine disk is over 85 % used (E) Ingestion lag Warning Ingestion lags by over 15 minutes (E)

The figures marked (E) are defaults. An administrator changes them in Settings > Agents and automations > Platform Health > Module thresholds (XTM One modes only; Edit, then Save), or with the Platform Health settings API (PUT /api/v1/health/settings, keys opencti.connector_stale_minutes, opencti.connector_errors_max, opencti.queue_depth_max, opencti.search_disk_max_percent, opencti.ingestion_lag_minutes); the next pass, within 5 minutes, reads them.

docs.title: OpenAEV checks
docs.text:
In XTM One mode, AI switched off included, every registered OpenAEV is checked every 5 minutes, with no enrolment, on the same rules as OpenCTI: the heartbeat reads the registration, the others read the health snapshot OpenAEV sends with its registration while it is under 15 minutes old. An OpenAEV release that sends no snapshot is only checked for its heartbeat.

Check Severity Fails when Heartbeat Critical OpenAEV has not registered for 15 minutes Healthcheck Warning, Critical OpenAEV reports a failing healthcheck of a type (mail server, agent or executor, security platform collector, injector contract, ...): critical when one is in error, a warning otherwise (one finding per type) Integration silent Warning An injector, collector or executor has not reported for 60 minutes (one finding per integration) (E) Agents offline Warning Over half of the agents are offline (E)

The figures marked (E) are defaults, changed like the OpenCTI ones, in the same Module thresholds block (keys openaev.integration_silent_minutes and openaev.agents_offline_max_percent).

docs.title: OpenCRQ checks
docs.text:
In XTM One mode, AI switched off included, every registered OpenCRQ is checked every 5 minutes, with no enrolment, on the same rules as OpenCTI and OpenAEV: the heartbeat reads the registration, the job check reads the health snapshot OpenCRQ sends with its registration while it is under 15 minutes old. An OpenCRQ release that sends no snapshot is only checked for its heartbeat.

Check Severity Fails when Heartbeat Critical OpenCRQ has not registered for 15 minutes Job failing Warning The last run of a background job ended in the dead-letter queue (one finding per job)

docs.title: Agent checks
docs.text:
Every 15 minutes, in every mode, the health pass checks the agents enrolled in Platform Health, and them alone: after an upgrade no agent is enrolled. These checks read counts, statuses and ids, never conversation content, and call no model. With AI switched off agents do not run, so they record nothing and an open finding is kept as it was.

Check Severity Fails when Assignment failing Warning The last 3 judged runs of an enabled assignment failed Schedule silent Info A slot of an enabled schedule came due more than an hour ago and nothing was recorded for it. A monthly or yearly schedule between two slots, or a schedule enabled again after its slots, is not reported Cost spike Warning A day's tokens are over 3 times the agent's daily average Owner disabled Warning The agent's owner account is deactivated Failure spike Warning Over 5 % of an assignment's last 20 settled runs failed Feedback drop Warning The agent's weighted feedback score is 10 points under the window before Cost drift Info The cost per run is up 20 % on the window before Model change Info The last day's runs used a model the 7 days before did not Integration broken Warning An integration bound to the agent is in error, must be re-authorized, or failed its last connection test Orphaned claims Warning A work item the agent owns is held by a run that ended Blocked without blocker Info A blocked work item the agent owns names nothing it waits for

The feedback drop, failure spike and cost drift checks read the thresholds of the signals. A finding resolves by itself after two passes in a row without its cause; pausing or deleting the assignment, or unenrolling the agent, resolves it too.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
The checks above are deterministic and never call a model. The analysis is an optional layer on top of them: one call to the platform routing model per module, which reads that module's open findings (check ids, severities, categories, subject ids and measured values; no conversation content) and writes a short explanation and the order in which to apply the fixes.

  • It is off by default, and runs only where AI runs (licensed, switched on).
  • A module is analysed only when its open findings changed, at most once a day, or when an administrator asks for it. A failed or refused analysis counts as that day's attempt: the schedule tries again the next day, and an administrator can run it at once.
  • A failed model call counts its full reserved cost against the ceilings, since a provider may bill a call that timed out.
  • It has a hard ceiling in tokens and in dollars, per day and per month. Before each call, the platform reserves the call's worst case on today and on this month; a call that would cross any ceiling is refused and the module shows Ceiling reached. After the call, the reservation is replaced by what the call really cost.
  • The default ceilings are 100,000 tokens and 1 USD a day, 3,100,000 tokens and 31 USD a month. They come from a measured run: one analysis of a module with 33 open findings cost 4,763 tokens; the most an analysis reads (60 findings) stays under 8,000 tokens, so the daily default covers two analyses of six modules.
  • A ceiling cleared to no value refuses every analysis (Ceiling not set).
  • Analysis calls are traced under their own source, Platform Health, visible in LLM analytics. They are not counted in any agentic quota or agentic execution count.
  • Analyse now does not re-run a check: it rewrites the explanation from the findings already stored. Run checks now on a module card runs that module's checks again and stores new evidence. A finding from a module check made by an older version of XTM One, or whose evidence is more than a day old, is marked as possibly outdated: the analysis never recommends a rollback, a restart or any other disruptive action from it and points to Run checks now instead.
  • After an upgrade, every registration with a finding from the previous check logic gets one new round of its module checks on its own, within the usual spend limits; until it lands, the API serves that finding with stale: true and the build that produced it (check_build).

Administrators switch the analysis on and set its four ceilings under Settings > Automations > Platform Health > Analysis. The Platform Health page shows an Analysis panel under the score history: today's and this month's spend against each ceiling, then each module's latest analysis (its explanation, or why it did not run: Ceiling reached, Ceiling not set, AI off, no routing model) and an Analyse now action, unavailable while AI is off or a ceiling is cleared.

The API is GET /api/v1/health/analysis (the latest analysis per module, the ceilings and the spend, and the Module Analyst's ceilings and spend under module_analyst) and POST /api/v1/health/analysis/{module}/run (an analysis now), both for administrators.

docs.title: Module Analyst spend limits
docs.text:
In the XTM One modes, the Module Analyst investigates each registered OpenCTI, OpenAEV and OpenCRQ read-only when its findings change and once a day, and attaches recommendations to the findings. It has its own ceilings, outside the agentic quota and outside the Platform Health budget above: tokens per cycle, tokens and dollars per UTC day and per calendar month. Its calls are traced as Platform Health and never counted in agentic quotas.

Administrators switch it on or off and set its five ceilings in the Module Analyst block of Settings > Agents and automations > Platform Health > Spend limits, next to the analysis; the block shows today's and this month's spend against them. The defaults are 80,000 tokens per cycle, 500,000 tokens and 4 USD a day, 10,000,000 tokens and 60 USD a month: a quiet cycle measured about 22,600 tokens per module. A model call that would cross a ceiling is refused and the cycle stops with what it has written; a ceiling cleared to no value refuses every call.

docs.title: Digest
docs.text:
Each cycle ends with a digest built from what the cycle actually did:

  • the memory consolidations (counts per operation, never the content);
  • the findings, new and already known;
  • the experiments, by outcome;
  • the proposals filed, applied and rolled back, and how many are unmeasured;
  • the budget spent (for a Module Analyst cycle, against its own ceiling);
  • for a Module Analyst cycle, the recommendations it attached, by confidence, and the agentic findings of its module opened and resolved;
  • everything skipped or not completed, with the reason (budget reached, a run that failed, experiments skipped).

A cycle reads Completed only when its run completed with nothing skipped. Otherwise it reads Partly completed, Budget reached, Failed or Cancelled. A figure that could not be read is shown as Unavailable, never as 0. The orchestrator's own report, written in the platform language, is shown under the figures.

The weekly digest assignment summarizes the cycles closed since the previous one, with a Modules part for the Module Analyst (cycles run, recommendations attached, agentic findings opened and resolved, spend against its ceiling); its result appears in the dashboard's latest results.

docs.title: The Platform Health page
docs.text:
Administrators find every proposal, cycle and signal on the Platform Health page (/health):

  • Improvements: every proposal, filtered by type and status, with its measured result, the number of writes simulated during its experiment, and its evidence. Evidence the viewer may not open is counted, not linked.
  • Cycles: every cycle and its digest; a Module Analyst cycle is listed as Module Analyst.
  • Signals: the signals currently crossed, and whether each started an investigation.

Managers see the proposals and cycles of the agents and flows they manage on those pages (see Platform Health).

docs.title: Chat with the orchestrator
docs.text: The Platform Health orchestrator answers in chat. With an administrator it reads every cycle and signal of its scope; with anyone else, only those of the agents and flows that person manages, and it may start an investigation on one of them on their behalf.

docs.title: Intents
docs.text:
Intents are the mechanism that makes XTM One agents appear inside the other XTM Suite products. A connected platform declares the AI capabilities it wants — summarize this container, translate this question into a search filter, process this bundle in a playbook — and you decide which agent answers each one.

Administrators choose Intents from the left sidebar to open the page.

docs.title: How routing works
docs.text:
An intent is a named capability, written in dotted notation, such as cti.container_summary or global.assistant. It says what has to be done, never who does it. The link between the two is a binding.

The full path from a click in OpenCTI to an answer from one of your agents looks like this:

  1. OpenCTI, OpenAEV, or OpenCRQ registers with XTM One and declares the intents it uses, along with its business vertical.
  2. XTM One adds any missing intent to the registry and tags it with the platform that declared it.
  3. You bind one or more agents to each intent, optionally scoped to a vertical and ordered by priority.
  4. A user triggers the feature in the platform. The platform asks XTM One which agents are bound to that intent for its vertical, and uses the one with the highest priority.
  5. The bound agent runs in XTM One with the context sent by the platform, and the result is returned into the product.

Step 3 is the one you control. Everything a user sees — or does not see — in another Suite product follows from it.

No binding, no feature

An intent that no agent is bound to is shown with an Unbound badge. The platform that declared it treats the corresponding feature as unavailable and usually hides or disables it. Binding an agent is what turns the feature on.

docs.title: Verticals
docs.text:
A vertical is the business coloration of a connected platform — cti, aev, crq, and, depending on the deployment, labels such as fimi or fraud. It lets the same intent resolve to a different agent depending on the context the request comes from.

The Verticals panel at the top of the page lists them all with the number of bindings that use them:

  • Verticals declared by a platform at registration are created automatically.
  • Administrators can add their own with Add Vertical.
  • Renaming a vertical updates every binding that uses it.
  • A vertical still used by a binding cannot be deleted.

A binding scoped to All verticals applies to every platform, whatever its business context. A binding scoped to one vertical only applies to platforms declaring that vertical.

docs.title: Bind an agent to an intent
docs.text:
From the Intents page:

  1. Expand the intent you want to serve.
  2. Choose Add Binding.
  3. Search for the agent.
  4. Select one or more verticals, or All verticals. One binding is created per selected vertical.
  5. Confirm.

You can do the same from the agent side: open the agent, go to Configuration, and use the Intent Bindings card. It shows every intent that agent already answers and lets you add or remove bindings without leaving the page.

An agent with the agent builder tools can do it from a conversation: list_agent_intent_bindings shows the intents an agent is bound to (vertical, priority, locked, built-in, default or personal) and whether a connected platform can be offered the agent at all, bind_agent_to_intent binds it (an intent name such as cti.stix_transformer, a vertical or all of them, a priority) and unbind_agent_from_intent removes a binding. The rules are the page's: an administrator writes the default binding, anyone else a personal override, a private agent is refused, a locked default is not overridden, and built-in bindings are not changed. get_agent lists the agent's bindings too.

The agent cannot be private

An agent exposed through an intent is offered to users of the connected platform, so it has to be company-managed or shared with at least one group. XTM One refuses every default binding to a private agent, whatever vertical it is scoped to, and a private agent is never offered to a connected platform even when someone binds it for their own use. Disabled agents are skipped too, even when a binding exists.

Some surfaces in the connected products list several agents for the user to choose from and filter that list by the product tag carried by the agent, such as opencti or openaev. Tagging your agent with the product identifier is what allows it to show up in those lists.

docs.title: Priorities when several agents share an intent
docs.text:
Several agents can be bound to the same intent. In that case the highest priority wins (in a vertical, the priority set for that vertical replaces the base priority), and on a tie the binding made first wins. Priority arrows appear next to each agent in the expanded intent card so you can reorder them. list_agent_intent_bindings and bind_agent_to_intent name the winner of each intent and vertical, with its priority, and the priority an agent needs to beat it.

Priority is evaluated per vertical. An agent can carry a base priority plus a per-vertical override, which is what you adjust when you move it up or down inside a vertical group. Bindings scoped to All verticals are listed inside each vertical group as well, since they compete with the vertical-specific ones.

To take over a capability that a built-in agent currently handles, bind your own agent to the same intent and vertical, then raise its priority above the built-in one.

docs.title: Built-in bindings
docs.text:
XTM One ships with a set of bindings that connect its built-in agents to the intents the Suite products declare. They are marked builtin and cannot be edited or deleted — they are restored at every startup, so a removed one comes back.

These are the shipped bindings:

Intent Capability Built-in agent Vertical global.assistant General-purpose assistant behind the in-product AI experience CTEM Assistant and XTM-One Assistant for all verticals, plus OpenCTI Assistant, OpenAEV Assistant, OpenCRQ Assistant, and FIMI Analyst on their own vertical all, cti, aev, crq, fimi global.summarize Summarize content OpenCTI Assistant, OpenAEV Assistant, FIMI Analyst cti, aev, fimi global.explain Explain content in simple terms OpenCTI Assistant, OpenAEV Assistant, FIMI Analyst cti, aev, fimi global.make_it_shorter Shorten content OpenCTI Assistant, OpenAEV Assistant, FIMI Analyst cti, aev, fimi global.make_it_longer Expand content OpenCTI Assistant, OpenAEV Assistant, FIMI Analyst cti, aev, fimi global.fix_spelling Fix spelling and grammar OpenCTI Assistant, OpenAEV Assistant, FIMI Analyst cti, aev, fimi global.change_tone Change the tone of content OpenCTI Assistant, OpenAEV Assistant, FIMI Analyst cti, aev, fimi cti.nlq_search Turn a natural language question into an OpenCTI filter OpenCTI NLQ cti cti.container_summary Summarize a container — report, grouping, case OpenCTI Entity Insights cti cti.container_report Write a report from a container — report, grouping, case OpenCTI Entity Insights cti cti.containers_digest Summarize the containers related to an entity OpenCTI Entity Insights cti cti.entity_activity Analyze the activity trend of an entity OpenCTI Entity Insights cti cti.entity_forecast Forecast the future activity of an entity OpenCTI Entity Insights cti cti.entity_history Summarize the internal history of an entity OpenCTI Entity Insights cti cti.stix_harvester Extract intelligence from a document into a STIX 2.1 bundle CTI STIX Harvester (Filigran AI) by default, CTI STIX Harvester as the lower-priority alternative cti cti.stix_transformer Enrich, filter, rewrite, or normalize a STIX 2.1 bundle CTI STIX Transformer on cti, FIMI STIX Transformer on fimi cti, fimi cti.stix_consumer Take a final action on a STIX 2.1 bundle at the end of a playbook CTI STIX Consumer cti cti.ttp_harvester Extract tactics, techniques, and procedures from documents CTI TTP Harvester (Filigran AI) aev aev.attack_path_orchestrator Drive a live, objective-driven attack path (AI penetration testing) in OpenAEV OpenAEV Attack Path Orchestrator aev aev.attack_path_additional_agent Specialist the attack-path orchestrator consults during an autonomous run - payload creation, code generation, recon, exploitation support OpenAEV Payload Creator aev aev.detection_rules_generator Generate detection rules from malware behavior AEV Detection Rules Generator aev aev.phishing_email_html_generator Generate phishing lure email HTML from a user prompt for authorized adversary-emulation exercises AEV Phishing Email Generator aev aev.phishing_landing_page_html_generator Generate phishing landing page HTML and CSS from a user prompt for authorized credential-capture simulations AEV Phishing Landing Page Generator aev aev.message_generator Generate messages for adversary emulation exercises OpenAEV Assistant aev aev.media_article_generator Generate media articles for adversary emulation OpenAEV Assistant aev

The Intents page is always the authoritative view for your own platform: it reflects what the connected products actually declared and what is bound today.

How the general assistant resolves

Several agents are bound to global.assistant. The CTEM Assistant carries the highest priority, so it is the one a connected product reaches first; it then hands the conversation over to the product specialist — OpenCTI Assistant, OpenAEV Assistant, or OpenCRQ Assistant. Bind your own agent above it if you want a different front door.

docs.title: Personal overrides
docs.text:
The bindings an administrator creates are the platform-wide defaults. A single intent can also carry a personal binding, which applies to that user's own requests only and leaves everyone else on the default.

A default binding can also be locked, which is how a capability is forced to resolve the same way for the whole organization. A locked default cannot be overridden, and an attempt to override it is rejected with a message stating that an administrator locked the binding.

docs.title: Custom intents
docs.text:
Administrators can add an intent with Create Intent, using dotted notation such as product.feature.action and a short description.

A custom intent is only useful when something asks for it by name — a platform that declares it at registration, or your own integration calling XTM One. Creating an intent no product asks for has no effect on what users see. An intent that has no binding left can be deleted; one that is still bound cannot.

docs.title: When a feature does not appear in a connected product
docs.text:
Work through this list when a user reports a missing AI action:

  • The intent shows an Unbound badge — no agent is bound to it yet.
  • The bound agent is disabled.
  • The bound agent is private, so it is never offered to platform users.
  • The agent is a copy of the bound one: a copy made with Duplicate or clone_agent has no binding of its own until you bind it.
  • The binding is scoped to a vertical the platform does not declare. Check the vertical on the platform's registration and either rebind to that vertical or use All verticals.
  • The intent is not listed at all, which means the platform never declared it. Confirm the platform is registered and running a version that requests that capability.
  • The user's own permissions on the connected platform do not allow the underlying operation.

For the user-facing side of the same question, see XTM One in OpenCTI and XTM One in OpenAEV.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Continue with Settings for the rest of the platform configuration, or read XTM One in the XTM Suite to see how these bindings surface for end users.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This chapter is for administrators. It covers the areas used to manage the platform, monitor usage, and configure shared settings.

docs.title: Administration is for
docs.text:
Use the administration sections when you need to:

  • review and route intents
  • manage users and groups
  • describe your organization for every agent
  • inspect platform objects and logs
  • adjust shared platform settings
  • stop every agentic activity at once with the emergency stop

docs.title: Intents
docs.text:
Intents connect user needs to agents. They are also how an agent becomes available inside OpenCTI, OpenAEV, or OpenCRQ.

Use this section when you want to:

  • review which intents exist
  • see which agents are bound to them
  • check which platforms declared them
  • adjust routing priorities
  • make one of your own agents answer a capability in a connected product

For most teams, this is the page that explains why one request reaches one agent instead of another. The Intents page covers bindings, verticals, and priorities in detail.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
The Users section is where administrators manage accounts: create a user or send an invitation, promote or demote, disable, enable or delete an account, reset a password or a two-factor enrollment, impersonate a user, set their quotas and review their API keys and activity.

See Users and groups for every task.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
Groups organize users: a resource shared with a group is shared with its members. A group also carries quotas, an AI switch and managers who follow its members' AI usage.

See Users and groups for every task.

docs.title: Switching AI off for a group
docs.text: The AI access card of a group turns AI off for its members. See Switching AI off for a group.

docs.title: Objects
docs.text:
Objects gives administrators a cross-user view of the platform's library entities, whoever owns them: agents, knowledge bases, prompts, skills, MCP servers, custom tools, integrations, presentations, videos (the Video Studio's, opened in their editor), templates, machines (the computers enrolled with XTM One Desktop or the headless runner), flows, datasets, evaluations, variables, channel bots and fleets (archived fleets included, marked Archived, the others with no status since whether a fleet runs is shown on the Fleets page; a deleted fleet is no longer an object and stays in the audit log). A type whose pages your deployment does not offer (Flows, Evaluations, custom variables, XTM One Desktop) is not listed either.

The library pages (Agents, Presentations, Templates, Flows, Evaluations, Variables, the XTM One Desktop page, and so on) list the same three tiers for everyone, administrators included: your own items, the items shared with you, and the items published to the whole company. Objects is where you find an item of one of these types that another person owns and has not shared.

Once you open an item, you see it whole, whoever owns it: an agent shows every integration, knowledge base, tool, skill, prompt, handover and assignment it is bound to, its runs, its chats and its delegations, and each of them opens and can be edited, as can the item itself. Reading the delegations of an agent that other users started (the consultations, transfers and background tasks on its Delegations tab carry their task descriptions and results) is recorded in Logs (action break_glass, entity Agent Delegations), naming the agent and the users whose delegations you read, one entry per administrator, agent and fifteen-minute window; your own delegations are not counted. The same holds the other way round: an integration, a knowledge base or a tool lists every agent that uses it. When you edit a colleague's agent, its pickers keep what the agent is already bound to, next to the items you can see yourself.

Use it to:

  • search any of these entities by name
  • filter by type or by owner
  • open any item directly (a row leads to the item's own page)

This is helpful when you need a cross-platform inventory, or when a user asks you to look at something they built, rather than a page-by-page review.

docs.title: Machines
docs.text:
Filter by Machines to see every computer enrolled with the platform, whoever enrolled it: how many there are, who owns each one, and whether it is still deployed. Each row shows the machine's operating system, whether it is Online, Offline (with the time it was last seen) or Revoked, and the version of the runner it runs. The connection state is the live one the XTM One Desktop page shows, not a stored flag, so a machine that stopped without disconnecting reads as offline here too.

Opening a row shows the machine's own page: its host details, its permission model, its pending approvals and its recent commands, with the same edit, revoke and delete actions an administrator has on the XTM One Desktop page. Reading the command history of a machine you neither own nor hold a configure-level share on (a view-only share is not enough - the full history then comes from your administrator role; a company-managed machine is yours to manage and is not counted) is recorded in Logs (action break_glass, entity Runner Commands): the commands carry shell output and file contents, so the trail says who looked at whose machine, one entry per administrator, machine and fifteen-minute window. Machines are not listed when the runner feature is disabled for the deployment.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Logs show the audit trail of user actions and important platform events: what was created, changed or deleted, by whom and when, and the configuration changes. When something changed and no one is sure why, this is usually the first admin page to check.

Narrow the list with:

  • the search box, which matches an entry's summary, the name of the item it is about and the email of the person who acted;
  • User, Action (for example create, update, delete) and Entity (the kind of item: agent, user, group and so on);
  • a date range.

The filters are kept in the address, so you can share a filtered view. Select an entry to open it as an Audit Log Event, with its full detail and the Raw Event (JSON), which you can copy.

Entries with the action break_glass record an administrator reading what belongs to someone else: the files of another person's conversation, the delegations of an agent other people started (entity Agent Delegations, see Objects), or the command history of a machine (entity Runner Commands, see Machines).

Audit log entries are kept for the Audit log retention (days) set in Settings > Observability, 90 days by default; the page says how long. An hourly job deletes older entries, except each user's most recent sign-in, which keeps their last login known. Deleting a user also deletes the entries of that user's own actions (see Users and groups). A user's own entries are also on the Activity tab of their page. Scripts read the log with GET /api/v1/audit-logs (administrators only; search, user_id, action, entity_type, date_from, date_to, limit up to 200 and offset).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings is where administrators configure the shared behavior of XTM One.

Common areas include:

  • AI models
  • general assistant behavior
  • channels and bots
  • integrations
  • quotas
  • MCP endpoint settings
  • security
  • observability
  • platform parameters
  • the organization profile (see Organization profile)

The Settings page covers those tabs in more detail.

docs.title: What may vary by deployment
docs.text:
The standard XTM One administration menu focuses on intents, users, groups, objects, logs, and settings.

Some deployments may include additional administration modules beyond this core set.

docs.title: What regular users should know
docs.text:
Regular users usually do not need the administration sections.

If you cannot see them, that is normal. Access is usually limited to administrators.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Continue with Intents to route capabilities to agents, Settings for the detailed platform configuration areas, or My profile for the settings users manage themselves.

docs.title: Organization profile
docs.text:
The organization profile describes your organization once, for every agent: what it does, where it operates, what it must protect, what it runs, how much risk it accepts and where findings become tickets. Agents read it before they rank, scope or estimate, so that a vulnerability, a threat or an exposure is weighed against your business rather than in general.

Administrators fill it in Settings > Organization. There is one profile per platform.

docs.title: How agents use it
docs.text:
Every agent has a read-only tool, get_organization_context, that returns the profile, in chat and in assignment runs alike. An agent that belongs to a fleet also starts each run with the profile in its context.

By default, every agent also starts each chat and each run with a short block: the organization's name, sector, regions, size and risk appetite, then one line per category of the profile with its size and the call that reads it. The categories are the long lists of the profile:

Category In the prompt Read with the tool Identity (name, sector, regions, size, risk appetite, currency) Always, in the short block The whole profile primary_assets, software, shipped_products, pirs, assets_exposure, tracked_organizations Their size, in the short block; their rows only when preloaded category, filtered by query, paged by offset and limit (up to 200 rows a page), so a list of any length is read whole. assets_exposure reads the merged assets of CTEM > Inventory (one row per real asset, with its sources and merged records) and its query also takes field:value terms on category, subcategory, criticality, internet_facing, os_family, source and group prioritization_policy Its number of rules, in the short block; the rules only when preloaded One row per threshold you set, per exclusion and per accepted risk enterprise_knowledge Its number of linked knowledge bases, never the content Without query, the linked knowledge bases; with query, the passages that answer it, only from the knowledge bases the person the agent acts for can read

A vulnerability on a product named like one of your imported GitHub or GitLab repositories (a CPE product part or a plain name, case, - and _ ignored) resolves to that repository in CTEM without a shipped_products row; forks are left out.

crown_jewels and tech_stack, the former names of primary_assets and software, are no longer read; a saved selection naming them was renamed on upgrade. The product list of an asset or an asset group, and the asset CSV column, are named products.

The short block stays the same size whatever the length of the lists. An agent asked about a vulnerability reads the software inventory page by page, or narrows it to a vendor or a product with query.

You choose at three levels, the most specific one winning:

  • Settings > Organization > Organization context in agents: Use organization context in every agent, on by default, and Preloaded organization categories, none by default, are the defaults for every agent and assignment.
  • An agent's Configuration > General: Organization context is Inherit (follow the platform), Always or Off; Preloaded organization categories is Inherit or a list of its own.
  • An assignment's parameters: the same two fields, Inherit following the agent, then the platform.

A preloaded category is loaded after the short block, capped, with the call that reads the rest. Each form shows the value in effect and where it comes from. Off on an agent or an assignment also removes the tool; the platform switch removes the short block only. A fleet run keeps its fuller profile block and does not repeat the short block. Every built-in agent inherits the platform default; the vulnerability and remediation agents of the exposure management fleets preload the software inventory, the primary assets, the assets and exposure, and the prioritization policy.

Agents cite the fields they used. For a field you have not filled, they name it in their output instead of guessing it: "the primary assets are not set", for example. The profile is treated as information typed by a person, never as instructions to the agent.

The profile also feeds other features:

  • An OpenCTI trigger can take its filters from the profile's intelligence requirements, regions and sector. See React to OpenCTI events.
  • The primary assets stay in line with OpenCRQ through a scheduled Inventory source (see Primary assets and OpenCRQ below).

docs.title: Shared context and permissions
docs.text:
The organization profile is one shared context for the whole platform. Every import, sync and agent write shows the same notice, Shared organization context:

  • Data is read from the source platform with the permissions of the person who sets up the import or sync. A sync keeps reading with the permissions of the administrator who saved it: the import dialog says Reads as or Runs as with that person, the Runs as column of Settings > Organization > Syncs names them, and editing a sync saved by someone else says whose permissions it runs with now and that saving it makes it run with yours (Runs as the owner, then Saving makes it run as you).
  • The source platform's access rules, including organization segregation and markings, are not carried over.
  • Once imported, the organization context is visible to every user and every agent of this XTM One platform.

This applies to the organization context only. Agent integrations, dashboards and every other feature keep each user's own permissions.

A CSV upload and a row typed by hand read no platform, so they carry the shared-visibility sentence only. The agent tools of the Organization context group (update_organization_context, upsert_organization_rows, run_organization_import, create_organization_sync, run_organization_sync, propose_organization_context_change) state the same in their description, and their previews and results carry the notice, so the agent tells the person before it applies.

docs.title: Let an agent edit the profile
docs.text:
Reading the profile needs nothing. Changing it is the Organization Profile Editing built-in tool group (organization_context), off by default and marked administrator-only in an agent's built-in tools:

  • update_organization_context saves field changes at once, on your profile or a tracked organization's: the whole new value of each field with its basis. Each value is validated like this form. The change is a new saved version authored by the administrator the agent acts for, the agent's name and the basis kept per field, so Saved versions below can roll it back. Each save writes an audit log entry.
  • propose_organization_context_change records a proposal an administrator accepts or rejects here instead.
  • list_organization_proposals and decide_organization_proposal read the proposals and accept or reject a pending one, as the review on this page does: accept names the fields or organizations kept, an empty list rejects it (a proposal already applied with update_organization_context, for example). A decided proposal is refused, and each decision writes an audit log entry.
  • list_organization_versions lists the saved versions of the profile, newest first, with their source, author and primary asset count; with version it reads that version's whole profile. restore_organization_version saves the next version with some fields (or every field) taken from a past one, with the same checks as the restore on this page, and answers the rows it drops; each restore writes an audit log entry.
  • update_organization_context and restore_organization_version take based_on_version, the version the agent read: when another version was saved since, nothing is saved and the agent is told to read the profile again.
  • reconcile_organization_with_opencrq runs the primary-asset reconcile with OpenCRQ of this page: apply false (the default) answers the plan, apply true saves a version of the profile. Nothing is written to OpenCRQ: the assets read are its primary assets.
  • upsert_organization_rows adds or updates rows of one section without resending the list. Assets and asset groups are keyed on the source the rows come from and their external_id there; a row a person wrote (source manual, csv or api) is never updated or removed, and a field the source does not send (owner, environment, group) keeps the value a person set. Software products are added when their name is new and never overwritten. Rows are validated like the CSV import; a bad row is refused with its reason and the others go on. At most 500 rows per call.
  • remove_organization_rows removes the assets or asset groups a source synced, by external_id (a device retired from the source).
  • run_organization_import runs the import of Draft the profile from your platforms for one section and one platform, with the same rules.
  • list_organization_syncs, create_organization_sync and run_organization_sync read, add and run now the scheduled syncs of Settings > Organization > Syncs (see Keep a section in sync). A sync an agent creates is saved with the administrator the agent acts for as its owner: its runs read the platform with that administrator's token, exactly as a sync saved in the dialog. The agent previews the import with run_organization_import first; create_organization_sync refuses what the scheduler could not run (an unknown section, a platform that cannot feed it, an unknown time zone) and a second Sync all schedule.

The row and import tools preview by default: they answer what would be added, updated, left unchanged, removed or refused, with the reasons, and save nothing. With apply set to true they save a new version, authored by the administrator the agent acts for, with the agent and the counts kept as the basis.

Only an administrator can add the group to an agent. The tools are offered only on a turn that acts for an administrator: the verified caller in chat, the run's acting user in an assignment. A non-administrator talking to the same agent does not get them, and a direct call is refused ("only an administrator can change the organization profile"); an identity the platform cannot resolve is refused too. The built-in CTEM Assistant and the Platform Health orchestrator keep their proposal tool without the group.

docs.title: Fill the profile with an agent
docs.text:
An agent bound to the integration (read-only is enough) and to Organization Profile Editing fills a section from any platform the integration reaches: an endpoint manager, an EDR, a cloud inventory, a CMDB.

Intune. Bind the agent to the Microsoft Intune integration and ask:

List every managed device in Intune with intune_list_devices (page through all of them),
then upsert them into the assets with upsert_organization_rows, source intune,
rows_format intune_device. Show me the preview first; apply only when I say so.

With rows_format intune_device the platform maps each device itself: the Intune device id is the external_id, the operating system gives the category (Windows, macOS and Linux devices are workstations, laptops when Intune says so; iOS and Android devices are smartphones, iPads tablets), and the operating system and compliance state become tags (os:windows, compliance:noncompliant). The primary user's name becomes the owner only when you pass include_owner true. With intune_detected_app, detected apps are reduced to the security products among them (Defender, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne and the like), added to the software inventory.

On a schedule. To keep the assets in sync, give the same agent an assignment with a schedule trigger (for example 0 6 * * *, every day at 06:00) and a prompt such as:

Read every managed device from Intune. Upsert them into the assets with
upsert_organization_rows, source intune, rows_format intune_device, apply true.
Then remove with remove_organization_rows the intune assets whose device id
Intune no longer lists. Report the counts and every refused row with its reason.

The run acts as the assignment's user, who must be an administrator for the tools to be offered. Each run saves at most one version per call, visible in Saved versions below.

A platform sync instead of an assignment. For a platform the import reads (OpenCTI, OpenAEV, OpenCRQ), the agent can schedule the platform sync itself, with no model call at each run:

Preview the OpenCTI import of the assets with run_organization_import. If it looks right,
keep it in sync every day at 06:00 Paris time with create_organization_sync, then
run it once now with run_organization_sync and report the counts.

In one click. On Settings > Organization, Draft > From a connected integration opens a dialog: pick a connected integration, turn on Keep the assets in sync every day if you want the scheduled assignment, then Open the chat. The chat opens with the agent and its preview instruction ready to send; nothing is saved until you confirm in the chat. The dialog calls POST /api/v1/organization-context/fill-agent, which, with an integration_id, creates that agent for you: bound to the integration read-only and to Organization Profile Editing, its persona and its first prompt written for the platform (Intune devices are mapped on the server, any other platform's devices are mapped by the agent with their own id as external_id). With schedule true it also creates the assignment Keep my assets in sync from (cron 0 6 * * * by default, timezone optional). A second call for the same integration reuses the agent and the assignment. The call creates nothing when AI is off or unlicensed.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: At the top of Settings > Organization, the Sources panel says who feeds the profile before the tabs say what it holds. It lists each connected platform (OpenCTI, OpenAEV, OpenCRQ) with its number of syncs, then the rows typed by hand, imported from CSV, written through the API or kept by an agent. Each source shows one chip per section it fills (primary assets, software inventory, assets, asset groups) with its number of rows; a chip opens that section's tab, filtered on the source where its table has a Source filter. Add a sync opens the import stepper: pick a section and a platform, preview the rows, then turn on Keep in sync. With no source yet, the panel says where to start.

docs.title: Edit the profile
docs.text:
Select Edit, change what you need, then Save. Cancel drops your changes.

Above the form, a box lists the fields not filled yet: the same list agents report. The fields are:

  • Organization name, Organization size (a band of employees), Sector and Sub-sector.
  • Regions of operation: two-letter country codes, separated by commas (FR, DE, US).
  • Annual loss threshold and Approval threshold: your risk appetite, as amounts.
  • Currency: a three-letter currency code (EUR), and Loaded hourly rate: the cost of an hour of your team's work.
  • Ticketing integration and Ticketing project: where CTEM cases become tickets (for example jira and SEC). The target counts as filled only when both are set. Both sit at the top of the CTEM case sync card, before the rules that say how a case opens, updates and closes its ticket.

The Priority intelligence requirements (PIRs) are not on this page: pick them on CTEM > Inventory > Exposure policy > Prioritization policy, next to the two PIR score thresholds (PIR score minimum: vulnerabilities and PIR score minimum: threat activity). The list is picked from the PIRs of your connected OpenCTI: it filters the two PIR playbooks and raises the context score of a threat or a vulnerability flagged in one. Select Edit on the card, change the list, then Save.

A value that is not valid (a region that is not a country code, an amount that is not a number) is refused, and the message names the field.

docs.title: Pause and resume CTEM case opening
docs.text:
The Case opening switch sits in the toolbar of CTEM > Cases, beside Group by and Views, and on the header of CTEM > Signals > Sources, for administrators. It is on by default. Hover it to see how many confirmed signals are waiting while it is off.

  • Off: a confirmed signal opens no case. It stays confirmed and waits; an empty Cases list says case opening is off. Case deadlines, announcements and the stall reminder keep running, and a case can still be split by hand.
  • On again: every waiting signal opens (or joins) its case at once, without waiting for the next scheduled pass, and the Cases list fills while you watch.

Other users do not see the switch. Every change is in the audit log.

docs.title: Primary assets and business services
docs.text:
The primary assets are the assets that matter most to the business. Without them, agents cannot rank findings by business impact. In edit mode, Add a primary asset adds a row with:

  • the primary asset's name;
  • the Business service it supports;
  • its Owner;
  • its Criticality: Low, Medium, High (the default) or Critical.

A link icon marks a primary asset linked to an OpenCRQ asset.

docs.title: Primary assets and OpenCRQ
docs.text:
OpenCRQ rates the same business assets as primary assets. With OpenCRQ connected as a company-managed integration, the primary assets are an Inventory source: CTEM > Inventory > Sources lists the OpenCRQ primary-asset sync next to the asset sources, with the same controls (enabled, schedule, last run with its counts, next run, Run now, errors). It is on and daily by default, and it links the supporting assets to their primary assets unless turned off.

  • A primary asset you add or edit by hand, and a link you add or remove by hand, always win over the sync.
  • Turning the source off stops the schedule; the rows it already wrote stay.

The primary assets card names the source with the OpenCRQ icon and the time of its last sync. It has no OpenCRQ button: run or configure the sync from Sources. OpenCRQ is read with the access of the administrator who last saved the sync. See XTM One in OpenCRQ.

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
The software inventory lists the products you run, so that agents can match vulnerabilities to them. Add a product adds a row with the Product, its Vendor and, optionally, its CPE: the standard product identifier that vulnerability records use, which makes the match exact.

When your assets carry their installed software (from a sync or an import), the software inventory agents read is built from it: one entry per product, with each version seen and the number of assets running it, and the sources that report it. The rows you typed stay: a product no asset reports (a SaaS application, a cloud service) keeps its own entry, and a CPE you typed wins over the one a source reports. GET /api/v1/organization-context/software answers the same list (the CTEM > Inventory > Software tab), and GET /api/v1/organization-context/assets/by-software?product= lists the assets running a product.

docs.title: Software from an SBOM
docs.text: An SBOM (software bill of materials) lists what an application or a container image is made of. An administrator can import one on an asset with POST /api/v1/organization-context/assets/{asset_id}/sbom (a CycloneDX JSON or SPDX JSON file in the file field): its components join the asset's software with the source sbom, with their CPE and package URL when the SBOM gives them, and with the component that bundles them (the NGINX inside an ingress controller image, for example). A component without a version is listed as unknown. Importing the same SBOM again replaces what it gave; another SBOM on the same asset adds to it. The SBOM stays with the asset when a sync merges it with another record. A file over 10,000 components is refused: split it per application or image.

docs.title: How one asset is matched across sources
docs.text: The same device read from two sources (an endpoint manager and OpenAEV, for example) is one asset when they share a strong identifier: hardware serial, cloud resource id, code repository path, managed device id, MAC address, FQDN or hostname, in that order by default. A code repository is matched on its path (github.com/owner/repo, read from its URL or from a name such as Owner/Repo, whatever the case or a trailing .git), so the repository OpenAEV lists and the one GitHub or GitLab sends are one asset; two repositories with different GitHub or GitLab ids are never merged on the path. An IP address alone never merges two assets. Each field shows the value of the source that ranks first for it (by default the endpoint manager or EDR for the operating system and software, OpenCRQ for criticality, OpenAEV for exposure), and every source's value is kept. An administrator can change the order of the identifiers, leave one out, or change the source order of a field in the profile's asset_identity part; GET /api/v1/organization-context/assets/identity shows the saved settings, the defaults and what applies.

docs.title: AI targets are assets
docs.text: The AI your organization runs or exposes is an asset of category AI target, as in OpenAEV, with its subcategory (LLM model, AI agent, MCP server or RAG pipeline), provider, endpoint, model and modality. It is listed, filtered and synced in CTEM > Inventory > Assets like any other asset, and AI security work reads it from there: an agent reads them with the assets_exposure category and the query category:ai_target. The profile has no separate AI list: entries saved in it before were turned into AI target assets, linked to their OpenAEV record when they had one.

docs.title: Saved versions
docs.text:
Each save is a new version: nothing is overwritten. The page shows the current version and when it was saved. When two administrators save at the same moment, the second save is refused: reload the page and save again.

Scripts list the saved versions, newest first, with GET /api/v1/organization-context/versions (administrators only). Any signed-in user can read the current profile with GET /api/v1/organization-context. The profile carries its own fields only: assets and asset groups are read and written with /api/v1/organization-context/assets and /api/v1/organization-context/asset-groups, and the profile answers how many there are in row_counts. A save or a restore never changes an asset row, and a row list sent with it is ignored and named in ignored_row_fields. Restoring a version brings back profile fields only: assets keep their own history in CTEM > Inventory.

docs.title: Draft the profile from your platforms
docs.text:
XTM One can propose a profile from what your connected platforms already hold:

  • OpenCTI: your organization's name, its first sector and your priority intelligence requirements;
  • OpenAEV: your security platforms (EDR, SIEM and others), as software inventory entries;
  • OpenCRQ: the supporting assets rated high or very high, as primary assets linked to their asset.

Only empty fields are filled: what a person typed always wins. Each filled field names the platform it came from, and a platform that is not connected or cannot be read is reported instead of failing the draft. Each platform is read with your own access. No model is involved.

The draft is a proposal, never a save. In Settings > Organization, open Draft > From the platforms: the form opens on the proposed values, each one named with its platform, and nothing is saved until you select Save. A platform that could not be read is named with a link to Settings > Integrations. Scripts use POST /api/v1/organization-context/draft.

docs.title: Import one section from a platform
docs.text:
Settings > Organization > Import from the platforms imports one section of the profile from one connected platform, with no model call, in five steps:

  1. What to import: assets, asset groups, software inventory, primary assets or PIRs. AI targets come in with the assets (category AI target).
  2. Source: the platforms that hold this section, shown with their logo. A platform that is not connected or not readable with your account is shown greyed, with the reason.
  3. Filters: each value is picked from the platform itself, never typed.
  4. Mapping: each profile field with the platform attribute it reads, its fallback, and an example taken from the platform. The fields the platform does not provide are listed: rows keep what you typed for them.
  5. Preview: the platform's own count, then the rows that would be new, updated, unchanged or skipped. Nothing is saved before Import. When the platform cannot be read, the preview says so with the reason: the permission the integration lacks (for example the CrowdStrike Falcon Host groups: Read scope), an integration that is not connected, an HTTP status or a timeout. A platform's own error text is never shown.
Section Platform Filters Assets OpenCTI labels, markings, author, creator, category, subcategory, criticality, exposure, environment, platform, created on or after Assets OpenAEV asset groups, tags, category, subcategory, criticality, platform Asset groups OpenAEV tags, name contains Asset groups Microsoft Intune (Entra device groups), Tanium (computer groups), CrowdStrike Falcon (host groups), ServiceNow (business services) name contains Software OpenAEV security platform type Primary assets OpenCRQ lowest criticality, tenant PIRs OpenCTI the PIRs to import

An asset group read from a platform brings its members, kept in sync at every run: an asset leaving the group in the platform leaves it here, a member added by hand stays. A member the inventory does not hold yet is counted as not in the inventory. Intune groups are the Entra ID security groups that hold Intune devices (user groups are left out); the Intune integration then needs the Graph permissions GroupMember.Read.All and Device.Read.All besides DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All. CrowdStrike needs the Host groups: Read scope. ServiceNow groups are the business services, their members the hardware CIs related to them in the CMDB. Import the assets of the same platform first: a group binds its members to the assets that platform brought.

OpenCTI Systems carry a category, a criticality, an exposure, an environment, an owner and a platform from the OpenCTI release that ships OpenCTI-Platform/opencti#19943; the import reads them. On an older OpenCTI those filters are hidden and every System takes the type you pick on the filters step, which is otherwise used only for Systems with no category. The owner falls back to the System's author; the platform and the markings are kept as platform: and marking: tags.

Every row of every list section (primary assets, software inventory, assets, asset groups) records where it comes from: its source (manual when typed, csv, api, agent:<agent id>, or the platform: opencti, openaev, opencrq), its id in that platform (external_id) and the sync that wrote it (sync_id). A primary asset saved with only its OpenCRQ link reads as a row of that platform.

An import can run again with the same or other filters. A row a previous import from the same platform wrote is updated, never duplicated, and the fields a person added that the platform does not send (a primary asset's business service and linked assets, an owner the platform leaves empty) are kept; a row typed by hand, uploaded as CSV or written through the API is never overwritten. Rows a previous import wrote that the platform no longer returns with these filters are listed as no longer in the platform: they are kept unless you switch on their removal. Each import is recorded with the platform, the filters and the time of the read. Scripts use GET /api/v1/organization-context/import/options, POST /api/v1/organization-context/import/preview and POST /api/v1/organization-context/import/apply (remove_gone removes the rows no longer in the platform).

An asset is one real thing whatever the number of platforms that report it. When a platform sends an asset named like a row another source wrote (typed by hand, or read from another platform), the import adds it as a second record of that asset instead of skipping it, and the asset list shows it once, with each platform it comes from and, for every field, which source set the value. Records are joined on their serial number, cloud resource id, code repository path, device id, MAC address, fully qualified name or host name; an IP address alone never joins two records. An administrator can merge records the keys did not join, or keep apart two records they joined (POST /api/v1/organization-context/assets/decisions, removed with DELETE on the same path and the decision id); both are kept across syncs and written to the audit log. A row typed by hand needs an external id before it can be merged or kept apart, because without one it is known only by its position in the list.

docs.title: Keep a section in sync
docs.text:
An import can also be saved as a sync that runs again on a schedule, so the profile follows the platform: on the import's preview, switch on Keep in sync and pick the schedule, then select Import and keep in sync (or Save the sync when nothing is new today). Only the sections the import feeds can be synced: assets, asset groups, software inventory, primary assets and PIRs. The name, sector, regions, size, currency, risk appetite and the other typed fields are never synced.

A sync keeps the source, the filters, the batch type, the choice for the rows that left the platform (removed by default: a deletion upstream deletes the row in XTM One; switch it off to keep them), its exclusion list (excluded_external_ids: the platform's rows it never imports, a stored copy included) and a schedule:

  • Hourly, at a minute of the hour.
  • Daily, at a time in a time zone.
  • Weekly, on a day at a time in a time zone.

A section can carry several syncs, for example one per source or one per filter set. Sync all is one more schedule that runs every enabled section sync in the order they were saved. Run now runs a sync at once without moving its next scheduled run.

Settings > Organization > Syncs lists them: the section, the source, the filters, the schedule, the last run (when, rows added, updated and removed, or its error on hover), the next run, the status (Enabled, Paused with its reason on hover, Disabled) and the enabled switch, with Run now, Edit (schedule and switch) and Delete on each row. Add Sync all appears once a section sync exists. Deleting a sync stops its schedule; the rows it imported stay in the profile.

Each run follows the import rules:

  • A run saves a new profile version only when something changed. The version names the sync and the administrator who saved it.
  • A row typed by hand, uploaded as CSV or written through the API is never overwritten.
