The webhook URL shown for an OAuth default belongs to that admin app. By default, a verified event it receives reaches every assignment it reached before: those whose agent is bound to an integration of that provider. With Require verified integration notifications on (or INTEGRATION_NOTIFICATIONS_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION=true) it reaches only the integrations running on that app (created with its OAuth defaults; for an integration created before XTM One recorded that, the one whose client ID is the OAuth default's) whose agent owner may use them, and for a GitHub App event, only integrations that record its installation or, recording none, whose own GitHub token sees it (read in the background: a delivery never waits on GitHub, and one reaching an integration whose installations are not known yet is handed over as before; an integration holding no usable token, or a token GitHub lists no installation for, receives none); the Security Audit reports the default, and each delivery that reaches an assignment the strict rule would leave out is logged. An integration on a user's own app receives its events through its own webhook URL, shown on the integration page. The webhook verifies an event with the webhook secret set on the OAuth default (for LinkedIn, its client secret). For a provider with no OAuth default, or with one that holds no webhook secret, an event is accepted without a check, as before: the delivery is logged, and the Security Audit names the provider and the assignments it can trigger. LinkedIn notifications sent to /api/v1/integrations/notifications/linkedin follow the same rule: that URL belongs to the same admin app, whose client secret verifies each notification. With no LinkedIn client secret configured, a notification is accepted unverified as before (logged and reported by the Security Audit), and dropped in strict mode.

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text:
Quotas is the platform-wide usage control area.

In XTM One, it is mainly about:

  • agentic execution quotas
  • license-driven limits
  • per-user or per-group quota overrides

Some other deployments also show extra quota types such as LLM proxy usage.

Use this tab when you need to understand whether the environment is operating under a shared license limit or a manually configured quota policy.

docs.title: How the limits read
docs.text:
• A limit on a user, a group, or the per-user default is what one user may spend in the period. 0 is a hard stop: the user cannot run any agentic action. This holds under a Filigran license too - a user blocked by a 0, their own, a group's or the per-user default, stays blocked even while the license pool still has room.
  • A platform-wide cap (the Platform-wide limit field, or a period of your Filigran license) caps every user combined. Empty means no cap, and a license period issued without a quota has none either. The field no longer accepts 0; a 0 saved by an earlier version is read as no cap, as it always was. What a platform-wide cap has counted is saved to the database with the rest of the quota usage, every few minutes, so a Redis restart or eviction does not start the period over: at most the last few minutes of usage before it are lost.
  • An empty field on a user or a group inherits: the user falls back to their groups, then to the per-user default. To lift the limit for a user or a group instead, turn on its Unlimited switch.
  • When a user belongs to several groups, the most permissive group limit applies, and an Unlimited group is the most permissive of all. A group whose field is empty sets nothing and does not take part.

The platform configuration API reports a license period without a cap as null, and a deployment with no allowance at all (Community Edition) as 0.

These rules apply to every value saved from this release on. A value saved by an earlier version keeps the effect it had until you save it again: a 0 under the license pool gives way to the pool, a group without a limit yields to a member's other group that has a number, and a user or group quota type holding no limit counts as Unlimited. Where saving such a value would change what it does, its quota card says so.

docs.title: Requests with no account
docs.text:
Some agentic requests have no XTM One account behind them: a message from someone without an account on a channel that allows anonymous users, a visitor of an agent's public chat widget, and a call to the global MCP endpoint (/mcp/global) made with the platform MCP key. They count against the platform-wide limits exactly like everyone else's requests - the periods of your Filigran license, or the Platform-wide limit - and against nothing else: no per-user default, user or group limit applies to them, since there is no user.

  • At the limit, the person gets This service is at capacity right now. Please try again later. rather than a message about quotas or licenses they have no way to act on. On a channel, it goes wherever the bot would otherwise have answered, like the message a Community Edition deployment answers with.
  • While the quota store is unreachable, they are refused like every agentic request in xtm_one mode, with This service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.; in copilot / dev mode they follow Quotas when their store is unreachable.
  • A request that never reached a model (no provider configured, a provider that could not be reached) gets its action back. Any other failure keeps it: the Agent Failure Pool below is an allowance per user, and there is no user to draw it from.
  • Where they show: the platform-wide usage of this page, and the platform-wide gauge of a user whose limit is the platform-wide pool, include them. They are never attributed to anybody - not in a user's own usage, the top consumers or the Agent Failure Pool card.

An assignment run that no user can be attributed to (a company-managed assignment saved before every assignment kept its owner, with no Run as user) counts the same way.

docs.title: Resetting the platform-wide usage
docs.text:
The license ceilings (or, in copilot / dev mode, the platform-wide limit) are compared with the platform-wide usage counters: every action on the platform, whoever ran it, in the current day, month and year. No administrator action resets those counters - in XTM One mode they are what the license sells, so Reset usage on a user's page only ever resets that user's own counters.

When a deployment needs its allowance back before the window turns over - typically a proof of concept that used it before the evaluation ended - Filigran support can issue a reset code. On the license banner at the top of the page, Enter a support code (administrators only) takes it, and the same dialog takes an Agent Failure Pool recharge code as well: the code says what it grants.

  • A reset code starts the platform-wide counters of the current windows again from zero: by default the agentic and sandbox counters (the two an agentic ceiling adds up) in the current day, month and year; Filigran can narrow it to some of those windows, or include the LLM proxy counter. Past windows are history and stay as they are.
  • The ceilings themselves do not change, and neither does any user's own usage or limit. A user whose own agentic limit is tighter than the license ceiling stays blocked by it until you reset that user with Reset usage on their page.
  • The confirmation names every counter that was reset, with what it held before.
  • A run already in progress when the code is redeemed and refunded afterwards gives its action back to the fresh counter (at most one per run).
  • Like every support code, it is verified on the spot with no outbound call, single-use, bound to this platform unless issued as global, and expires on its own. It is recorded in the audit log (Reset the platform-wide usage counters (...) with support code ...) and, when the Agent Failure Pool card is shown, in its list of redeemed codes, marked Usage counters reset.

docs.title: Agent Failure Pool
docs.text:
An agentic action is deducted from the user's action quota before the agent starts, so a run that fails has already spent an action on work nobody received. The Agent Failure Pool card is where that is accounted for: each agent's first few failures are credited back instead of deducted, and the card shows how much of that allowance each agent has spent, how many pools are exhausted (and therefore spending actions on failures again), and the date the allowance renews.

The allowance renews once a year, on your Filigran license anniversary. Its size is set by the operator in the environment and is deliberately not editable here — it decides what is billable.

The pool only concerns users who have a limit to give back to. When a user's agentic quota is unlimited at every level — no license ceiling or platform limit, no default per user, no limit on the user or their groups — a failed run costs them nothing, so their agents' pools are left untouched. The card says so: a notice appears when the platform-wide quota is unlimited (the pool then only applies to users or groups carrying a limit of their own), and a row belonging to such a user reads Not applicable instead of Spent. It is never counted under Pools exhausted.

The credited-back totals count every credit granted in the window, including those of a user and an agent that have both been deleted since: those have no row left in the list, and the card says how many of the total they account for (including N for deleted users and agents), so the per-cause breakdown under each total always adds up to it.

Resetting a user's quota usage (Reset usage on the user's page) gives their agents a full allowance again: their credits leave the totals, and their causes leave the breakdown with them. Causes recorded by earlier versions cannot be traced back to a user, so a reset that removes credits from the current window files those older causes under No cause recorded rather than leave a breakdown larger than its total.

A reset, a support-code recharge or a support-code reset of the platform-wide usage never runs while quota usage is being saved to the database: the save in progress stands aside, usually within a fraction of a second. On the rare occasion it cannot, the action is refused with Quota usage is being saved right now, so nothing was changed. Try again in a few seconds., and a support code refused that way is not used up. A reset or a recharge that fails part-way leaves every counter as it was; the causes it had already removed from the breakdown then read No cause recorded.

The card separates the two reasons an action comes back, because only one of them is rationed:

  • Agent failure — the run failed on its own merits. This spends one slot of that agent's allowance, and the per-agent table shows how many slots are left.
  • No LLM call — the run never reached a model: the provider was unreachable, down or not configured, or the platform abandoned the work itself (worker lost, deadline blown) — assignment runs and background sub-agent tasks alike. Credited back for free, outside the allowance, however often it happens: no LLM was called, and an incident on the platform's side must not ration what a user gets. The Provider column counts those per agent.

Some agents carry a Platform badge. Those are the seeded platform automations, whose scheduled runs never consume the action quota at all — so they can never appear here for that work. A row exists for one only because someone triggered it manually, which is charged like any other run.

One action is available: Enter a support code. Filigran support can issue a single-use code that gives every agent on the platform a full allowance again without waiting for the renewal date — after an incident on their side, for instance. Paste the code (XTMP-…) and it is verified on the spot, with no outbound call; a refusal explains itself (not issued by Filigran, expired, issued for another platform, already used). Codes already redeemed are listed underneath with the date and the administrator who used them.

docs.title: MCP Endpoint
docs.text:
MCP Endpoint is the admin version of MCP exposure.

It lets administrators:

  • generate or revoke the global MCP key
  • copy the platform MCP endpoint
  • choose which agents are exposed globally
  • review the connection snippet for external clients

This is the shared endpoint, separate from the personal MCP exposure available in My Profile. A call made with the global MCP key has no account behind it: it counts against the platform-wide agentic limits (see Requests with no account). A call made with an OAuth token counts against its user's limits, like any other request of that user.

The page also contains the Platform MCP Servers card, which controls the native OpenCTI, OpenAEV, and OpenCRQ MCP servers (/mcp/opencti, /mcp/openaev, /mcp/opencrq):

  • a global enable/disable toggle (on by default)
  • the endpoint URL and live connection status for each platform

These servers activate automatically when a platform is registered with XTM One and expose business and knowledge tools only. See Platform MCP servers for details.

A separate Platform Tools MCP Server card controls /mcp/xtm, which exposes XTM One's own tools — agent traces, agents, assignments, runs, knowledge bases, prompts, skills, custom tools, integrations, and variables — to external MCP clients:

  • a global enable/disable toggle, off by default
  • the endpoint URL, with a copy button

It is off by default because it exposes this instance's configuration surface rather than a connected platform's content. Each caller only reaches what they can already see and manage in the UI, and every write goes through the same permission gates as the REST API.

Once enabled, the card also offers downloadable installer packages (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Agent Plugins) — the same ones users get in their profile, so you can review exactly what is handed out. With One-click install on, a download creates a new personal API key for the downloading user and writes it into the package; those key creations appear in the audit log like any other, and revoking a key cuts off only the client it was made for. See Platform tools MCP server for details.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Security is where administrators check the platform's security posture, set its security options and tool approvals, configure sign-in, connect secret vaults, review personal API keys and hold the emergency stop token. It has eight sections, each with its own address:

  • Security audit (/settings/security, the section the tab opens on)
  • Security options (/settings/security/options)
  • Tool approvals (/settings/security/approvals)
  • Authentication (/settings/security/authentication)
  • Secret vaults (/settings/security/vaults)
  • API keys (/settings/security/api-keys)
  • Emergency stop (/settings/security/emergency)
  • Memory purge (/settings/security/memory)

docs.title: Security audit
docs.text:
The security audit reviews the configuration the platform runs with: encryption, sign-in (SSO, self-registration, local sign-in, two-factor coverage, password, session and link lifetimes, the automations of accounts nobody signs in to), the platform registration token and the registered platforms (any the integration catalog does not list), integrations, agents and the public chat widget, channel bots, runners, relays, webhook assignments, custom tools and their sandboxes, the code interpreter, MCP and A2A, LLM providers and traces, and the infrastructure (Redis and the fail modes, debug mode, CORS, the reverse proxy). Each check reports a finding with a severity:

  • Critical - exploitable now: a secret everyone knows, a dependency failure that switches protections off.
  • Warning - a protection is off or misconfigured while what it protects is in use, or a setting silently weakens one.
  • Info - a protection is off with nothing it protects in use, a protection only monitors, or context.
  • Passed - enforced, or nothing to fix. A check that can warn also reports its pass whenever what it protects is in use, so the report shows what is enforced, not only what is not.

"In use" means the audit sees something the protection would refuse or change right now: an embedded widget, a webhook assignment with no secret, a stored OAuth token URL on loopback, runner or MCP credentials issued while the platform is served over plain HTTP, the answers or tool results a connected prompt guard does not evaluate. While it is in use, a protection that is off is a Warning, one that only monitors is Info, one that is enforced is Passed. An opt-in protection off with nothing in use is Info: a deployment that changed nothing is not warned about it.

The page shows:

  • the overall posture: At risk while a critical finding remains, Needs attention while a warning remains, Healthy otherwise, and how many security controls are enforced (and how many only monitor);
  • the pass rate, the share of the checks that passed. Informational findings neither pass nor fail, so they are not counted;
  • how many findings there are per severity, and per category with the category's own pass rate. Select a category to show only its findings;
  • two views, Findings and Controls. The address keeps the one you opened (/settings/security/audit?view=controls), so you can link to it;
  • the findings, grouped by severity or by category, which you can filter by severity, category and text. Each one says what was found and, when there is something to do, how to fix it;
  • when the audit last ran.

The audit reads the live configuration every time it runs. After changing a setting or an environment variable (and restarting the platform when the variable needs it), select Re-run to check the result.

The platform also runs the audit on its own once an hour. A Critical or Warning finding it has never reported notifies every active administrator in the notification bell: one notification per run, naming the new findings, which opens the audit on them. Each finding is reported once, for good: it is not reported again when it escalates, disappears and comes back, or when Redis restarts, since what was reported is kept in the database. A run with no active administrator records nothing, so the first administrator still hears about every finding. The only finding reported a second time is a dismissed one that reopens (see below). The notification names the findings only; what they list (accounts, agents) stays on this page.

docs.title: Dismissing a finding
docs.text:
Some findings describe a choice you made on purpose: a protection you leave off, a setting the deployment needs. Select Dismiss finding on a Critical, Warning or Info finding to accept it, with an optional reason (up to 1,000 characters). A dismissed finding:

  • leaves the counts, the posture, the pass rate and the category breakdown, and no longer raises its control in the Controls view;
  • is never notified;
  • is listed under Dismissed findings at the bottom of the Findings view, collapsed, with who dismissed it, when, and why. Restore counts it again; a restored finding that was never notified is notified once, like a new one. The platform keeps who last dismissed a restored finding, at which severity and why, along with who restored it and when.

A dismissal holds for the severity it was made at. When a later run reports the finding at a higher severity (an Info that became a Warning, a Warning that became a Critical), it reopens: it counts again at once, and the finding says it was reopened, from which severity, and shows the dismissal it replaced. The next hourly run records the reopening and notifies every administrator once (dismissing or restoring any finding in the meantime records it too). Dismiss it again if the new severity is acceptable too.

Dismissals are stored in the database, apply to every administrator, and are recorded in the audit log (dismiss and restore by the administrator who made them, reopen by the platform). Scripts use PUT /api/v1/security-audit/findings/{id}/dismissal with an optional reason and DELETE on the same address to restore; both return the report. In the report, a dismissed finding carries dismissed (who, when, why, and the severity it was dismissed at), a reopened one carries reopened, and dismissed_count says how many were left out of summary and score. A finding the audit does not report now cannot be dismissed, nor can a Passed one.

docs.title: Accounts nobody signs in to
docs.text:
Deactivating an account in Administration > Users and groups > Users pauses the assignments and flows it owns, except company-managed ones, and reactivating it resumes them unchanged. Removing someone from the identity provider only stops their sign-in: their account stays active, and so do their automations, with their identity and their integrations. authentication.dormant_account_automations is a Warning that lists the active accounts that own an enabled assignment (on an enabled agent) or an active flow that is not company-managed, when nobody has signed in to them for 30 days, or ever for an account created more than 30 days ago: each with its last sign-in and what it owns. Deactivate the account of anyone who left, or transfer the agent (its assignments follow) or the flow to an active owner, or make it company-managed. While every such owner signed in within 30 days, the audit reports authentication.automation_owners_signed_in instead.

A sign-in is one the audit log records: a password (with its second factor when there is one), OIDC or SAML, an MCP OAuth authorization, or an XTM One Desktop sign-in confirmed in the browser (declining one is not a sign-in). A session lasts the absolute session lifetime (JWT_EXPIRE_MINUTES, 7 days by default) and is not extended, so anyone using the web app signs in within the 30 days unless that lifetime is set longer. API keys and the chat embedded in OpenCTI or OpenAEV do not sign in: an account used only through them is listed too.

docs.title: Personal API keys
docs.text:
Personal API keys (fcp-...) authenticate their owner on the REST API, the LLM proxy and the MCP endpoints, so the audit reports the ones that authenticate today (active, unexpired, of an active account):

  • authentication.api_keys_without_expiry (Info): keys that never expire, while no maximum lifetime is set. Set API key maximum lifetime (days) in Security options (API_KEY_MAX_LIFETIME_DAYS).
  • authentication.api_keys_beyond_max_lifetime (Warning): once a maximum lifetime is set, the keys that never expire or expire more than that many days from now, later than a key created or re-dated today may. Setting the maximum never cuts an existing key off: a key created before it keeps its expiry, or none, until its owner gives it one in My Profile > API Keys or an administrator revokes it.
  • authentication.api_keys_expire (Passed): every active key expires, within the maximum lifetime when one is set.
  • authentication.api_keys_full_scope (Info): keys that reach every surface, read-write, for every agent - all their owner can do. Every key created before scopes existed is one, until it is changed. authentication.api_keys_scoped is the pass.

Each lists the keys by name, owner and last use, and Review these API keys opens API keys filtered on them.

docs.title: Nova semantic thresholds
docs.text: The semantics: thresholds of the Nova community rules were written for all-MiniLM-L6-v2. The platform scores them with its own embedding model and maps each score onto that model's scale when the model has a measured calibration (see Semantic-threshold calibration). While the Nova integration runs its full engine and an enabled platform rule has a semantics: pattern, the audit reports agents.nova_semantics_calibrated (Passed) on a calibrated model. On a model with no calibration it reports agents.nova_semantics_uncalibrated_block_rules, a Warning listing the Block rules among them, or agents.nova_semantics_uncalibrated, an Info, when they all only log. Switch those rules to Log on the Nova rules tab, or pick a calibrated embedding model for the semantics tier there. When the semantic model picked there is not used (chosen for another embedding provider, or returning no embedding), it also reports agents.nova_semantic_override_ignored, a Warning, and the findings above describe the platform embedding model the tier scores on instead.

docs.title: Reads with no account
docs.text:
An agent that browses the platform (the agent builder's read tools, template search) for a caller with no account - an anonymous channel sender, the public chat widget - sees only company-managed resources without Restrict access; what the agent itself is configured with stays its reach (see Channels). Three kinds of work with no account keep every company-managed resource, restricted ones included, and three Info findings list them while a company-managed resource has Restrict access on:

  • access.ownerless_assignments_restricted_reach: company-managed assignments that run with no user (an automatic trigger and no "run as" user) - set a "run as" user in each resource's audience;
  • access.global_mcp_key_restricted_reach: the agents the global MCP endpoint's platform key runs - expose there only agents meant for every key holder;
  • access.ownerless_evaluations_restricted_reach: evaluations with no owning user - give the evaluation an owner in each resource's audience.

docs.title: Personal credentials used by others
docs.text: An integration connected with a person's own credential - a connected account, a personal access token, an API key - lends it to everyone who can act with it: the people and groups the integration is shared with (a connected account only once its holder shared it), and the audience of every agent, assignment, flow, knowledge base, skill or General Assistant list holding it, whose runs use it as bound (of an agent bound to it, the people who can start one of its runs and its callers without an account: the people who only chat with it and cannot see the integration use their own). access.personal_credentials_lent is an Info finding listing each such integration, whose credential it is, through what it is lent and how many people (or a public widget link, people with no account on a channel, the holders of the platform MCP key) act with it; it also lists an integration whose owner acts with an account the previous owner connected. A company-managed integration's credential is the company's and is not listed. Review each in the integration's Sharing and access section, and where others should not act as its holder, turn on Don't share my connected account, switch the agent to per-user integrations, or give the work a company-managed integration.

docs.title: Tool approvals
docs.text:
The two switches of Tool approvals are controls, agents.tool_approvals and agents.tool_approvals_default, and the audit reports which tool calls ask first:

  • agents.tool_approvals_off: a Warning while approvals are off for the whole platform and an agent, or the General Assistant, would otherwise ask; agents.tool_approvals_off_unused is the Info when none would. agents.tool_approvals_on is the pass.
  • agents.tool_approvals_default_off: an Info listing the agents that follow a platform default that asks for nothing (approvals are opt-in, so a new install starts that way on purpose and it never raises a security notification); agents.tool_approvals_default_on is the pass. agents.tool_approvals_agents_opted_out (Info) lists the agents set to Don't ask.
  • While something asks, the tools that run without asking anyway: agents.tool_approvals_bots_trusted (Warning, the channel bots set to run their tools without approval), agents.tool_approvals_platforms_skip (Warning, the connected platforms whose tools run while no prompt can be shown), agents.tool_approvals_users_allow_all (Info, how many users turned on Allow every tool for me) and agents.tool_approvals_whitelist_additions (Info, the tools that may change data an administrator let run without asking under Tool rules).

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
A security control is one switch that makes the platform safer when set: an environment variable, or a setting stored in Settings. The Controls view lists every control that applies to this platform (the SSO controls, for example, only once SSO is on) with its state:

  • Enforced - set to the value that protects.
  • Monitoring - it records what it would block without blocking it. The tool-call budget is one: without the strict cut, a batch that crosses the budget still runs, and the overshoot is logged and recorded on the run's trace. The content security policy is another in its default report-only mode: browsers block nothing and report what it would block (see Security headers).
  • Off - neither.

Each control shows its setting, its current value next to the value that enforces it, Opt-in when the platform default leaves it off, and the most severe finding about it. A control that is off while a warning or a critical finding is about it comes first, then the other controls that are off, then those that monitor and those that are enforced. Open a control to read what enforcing it changes for users, where what it would block is recorded (read it before enforcing), how to change it, the platform default and the findings about it. Filter the controls by state, category and text.

A control set by an environment variable is changed by setting the variable and restarting the platform; a stored control is changed on the Settings page it names, and a per-agent control (visitor uploads on the public chat widgets) on each agent it counts. A control that is also one of the security options can be changed there too, with no restart: its details say where its value comes from (its environment variable, a value saved in Security options, or the default) and link to the field (Configure <option>), unless its variable is set - the control then shows the Env badge, since the variable wins. A control XTM One fixes, the quota fail mode, is always enforced in xtm_one mode: its details say it cannot be changed.

Control Setting Enforced when What enforcing it changes authentication.api_key_max_lifetime API_KEY_MAX_LIFETIME_DAYS 1 to 365 A personal API key created or given a new expiry from then on must expire within that many days, and one created without an expiry gets the longest allowed. Existing keys keep the expiry they have: the Security audit lists those that outlive the limit, for their owner to re-date or an administrator to revoke. authentication.invitation_expiry INVITATION_EXPIRE_HOURS <= 168 An invitation link lasts a week at most unless the administrator who creates it picks another lifetime: an invitee who waits longer needs a new one. authentication.local_sign_in local_auth_enabled in Settings > Access and security > Authentication (Local Authentication) false Every sign-in goes through SSO, administrators included: password sign-in and self-registration are refused (an invitation still registers its invitee). Keep an administrator who signs in through SSO before turning it off, since an identity provider outage then locks everyone out. authentication.min_password_length MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH >= 12 A password set from then on (registration, invitation, password change, a local account an administrator creates) needs at least that many characters, with a letter and a digit as today. Existing passwords keep working until they change. authentication.password_reset_expiry PASSWORD_RESET_EXPIRE_HOURS 1 A password reset link stops working an hour after it is sent: someone who opens the email later asks for a new one. authentication.platform_token_audiences XTM_AUTH_ACCEPTED_AUDIENCES empty A token a registered OpenCTI, OpenAEV or OpenCRQ signs a user in with is accepted only when it is addressed to BASE_URL, XTM One's identity (published at /xtm/auth/metadata): a platform version that addresses its tokens to the internal URL it reaches XTM One on is refused until it reads that document. authentication.self_registration registration_enabled in Settings > Access and security > Authentication (Allow local registration) false Nobody can create an account from the sign-in page: accounts come from an administrator, an invitation or SSO. authentication.session_idle_timeout SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES 5 to 30 A session nobody uses for that long ends: the web app signs the person out and they sign in again. Clicking, typing, scrolling or coming back to the tab counts as use; what the web app does on its own (refreshing a page, the activity stream, an answer streaming in the chat) does not. The web app warns a minute before. While Redis cannot be reached, sessions are not ended for inactivity. authentication.session_lifetime JWT_EXPIRE_MINUTES <= 1440 People sign in again at least every day, even while they use the platform (through their identity provider with SSO), and a stolen session token stops working within a day. Lowering the lifetime ends the sessions already older on their next request; raising it applies from the next sign-in. API keys and platform tokens are not sessions and are not affected. authentication.sso_account_creation oidc_auto_create_users, saml_auto_create_users, allowed_domains in Settings > Access and security > Authentication (On-the-fly user creation, Allowed email domains) false, or allowed email domains set SSO no longer creates an account for everyone the identity provider authenticates. With On-the-fly user creation off, only people who already have an account, matched by SSO subject or email, can sign in through SSO; anyone else is refused until an administrator or an invitation creates the account. With allowed email domains set, SSO creates an account only for an email address, as the identity provider asserts it, at one of those domains. Existing accounts keep signing in whatever their domain. With XTM_HUB_ADMIN_GROUP set, the XTM Hub decides who may sign in through OIDC. authentication.sso_auto_admin oidc_auto_admin_new_users, saml_auto_admin_new_users in Settings > Access and security > Authentication (Automatically admin users) false People who sign in through SSO keep the role an administrator gave them. While it is on, everyone who signs in through that method is made an administrator, existing accounts included and at every sign-in; turning it off demotes nobody. With XTM_HUB_ADMIN_GROUP set, the XTM Hub decides the role of an OIDC sign-in instead. agents.tool_result_guard_scope PROMPT_GUARD_SCANNED_TOOLS the tools that return outside content While a prompt guard (Nova) is connected, it evaluates what the listed tools return to an agent, the text of the files they attach included, and records each rule match in the audit log. The evaluation runs beside the agent, so it adds no wait unless tool results a block rule matches are also withheld. agents.tool_result_guard_blocking PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_TOOL_RESULTS true A screened tool result that a block rule matches is withheld: the agent reads a short refusal naming the tool instead, without the files the result carried. The agent then waits for the guard's verdict on each screened result before it continues. Monitoring while tools are screened and it is off: each match is recorded, the result reaches the agent. access.agent_tools_strict_admin_access AGENT_TOOLS_STRICT_ADMIN_ACCESS true An admin's agent tools (the agent builder in chat and on the XTM One MCP server, the work-items delegation) read, trigger, edit, delete or add assignments only where the admin's own, group-shared and company-managed objects reach; admins keep full access through the UI and the REST API. access.presentation_public_links PRESENTATION_PUBLIC_LINKS_ENABLED false Nobody can open a presentation without an account: every public link answers as if it did not exist, at once, and neither the Share dialog nor an agent can create one. The links are kept, so turning the option back on brings back those that were not turned off. access.video_public_links VIDEO_PUBLIC_LINKS_ENABLED false Nobody can watch or download a video without an account: every public video link answers as if it did not exist, at once, and neither the Share dialog nor an agent can create one. The links are kept, so turning the option back on brings them back. access.dashboard_public_links DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_LINKS_ENABLED false Nobody can open a custom dashboard without an account: every published link answers as if it did not exist, at once, and none can be published. The links are kept, so turning the option back on brings them back. Off by default. agents.scheduled_work_items SCHEDULED_WORK_ITEMS_ENABLED false No agent can schedule a one-off action from a chat and nothing already scheduled is run: every agent's scheduling tools answer that scheduling is disabled by the administrator. Items that come due meanwhile are marked missed and their creators notified; turning the option back on lets them reschedule. Recurring assignments are not affected. agents.prompt_guard_blocks_general_assistant PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_GENERAL_ASSISTANT true While a prompt guard (Nova) is connected, a General Assistant message one of its block rules matches is refused with the guard's message before the model is called, instead of being answered. A false positive refuses a colleague's question. agents.prompt_guard_blocks_public_widget PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_PUBLIC_WIDGET true While a prompt guard (Nova) is connected, a public chat widget message one of its block rules matches is refused with the guard's message before the model is called, instead of being answered. A false positive refuses a visitor, who has nobody to ask. agents.prompt_guard_model_output PROMPT_GUARD_MODEL_OUTPUT block While a prompt guard (Nova) is connected, every model answer is evaluated before it is delivered, and one of its block rules matches is replaced by a withheld notice: answers take the evaluation's time longer. A streamed answer (web chat, the streaming chat embedded in OpenCTI / OpenAEV, the widget's stream) has already been shown, so it is only audited. log is the monitoring state. agents.tool_approvals tool_approvals_enabled in Settings > Access and security > Tool approvals true A tool call that asks first waits until a person approves it, in chat and in assignment runs, for every agent that asks before running tools. Suspended, no tool call waits for anyone and tools that change data run without asking; the tool rules, the connected platforms' policies and every personal approval are kept for when approvals resume. agents.tool_approvals_default approve_tool_calls_default in Settings > Access and security > Tool approvals (Every agent asks by default) true Every agent that follows the platform default, and the General Assistant where chat is available, wait for a person to approve each tool call that asks first; an agent set to Ask or Don't ask keeps its own choice. Tool approvals are opt-in: a new install starts with it off, and an upgrade keeps the value already stored (on where an administrator, or an earlier release creating the settings, turned it on), so that no running agent starts asking on its own. Listed only while tool approvals are not suspended. network.trust_proxy_headers TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS false X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto count only from a proxy FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS names, never from any peer. Declare the proxy there first: without it, rate limits bucket every caller under the proxy's address and HTTPS behind it is unconfirmed. network.client_ip_strict CLIENT_IP_STRICT true Every client address is keyed, logged and stored in canonical form - port, brackets and IPv6 zone index dropped, an IPv4-mapped address read as IPv4, IPv6 lowercase - so one client is one rate-limit key whatever the proxy wrote. A client whose address arrived in another spelling has its current rate-limit window restart once. network.rate_limit_ipv6_prefix RATE_LIMIT_IPV6_PREFIX <= 64 The per-IP rate limits key a native IPv6 client on its network (its /64 at 64) instead of its address, so rotating addresses within it draws no fresh bucket. Every device of one /64, a corporate IPv6 LAN included, then shares one budget. network.credential_transport_strict CREDENTIAL_TRANSPORT_STRICT true Runner enrollment (POST /runners/enroll), MCP OAuth client registration (POST /mcp/oauth/register) and the MCP OAuth token endpoint (POST /mcp/oauth/token) refuse a request the platform cannot confirm arrived over HTTPS - 403 https required, the OAuth invalid_client_metadata error and the OAuth invalid_request error - instead of serving it. Behind a TLS-terminating proxy, FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS must name it first, or every runner enrollment, MCP client registration and MCP token request through it is refused; a deployment served over plain HTTP can no longer enroll runners, register MCP clients or issue MCP tokens. network.relay_version_floor RELAY_MIN_SUPPORTED_VERSION a relay version (e.g. 1.261002.1) A relay older than the floor is refused when it connects and asked to update: one that updates itself does so at its next check, one in a container needs a newer image. Until then its group carries no request through it. network.secret_vault_trusted_origins SECRET_VAULT_TRUSTED_ORIGINS empty A vault connected in Settings > Access and security > Secret vaults is never reached on a loopback address; only a vault on the platform's own host (a Vault Agent, a 1Password Connect server beside it) needs its origin listed. Link-local and cloud metadata addresses stay refused whatever the list holds, and vaults declared in the environment are not affected. See Secret vaults. web.content_security_policy CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_MODE enforce Browsers refuse to run a script or load a resource the platform's pages do not need, a script injected past the output checks or added by a proxy or CDN included, and to show the pages in the iframe of a site the policy does not allow. The API reference, the Teams tab and the Office add-in stay report-only. web.cors_origins CORS_ORIGINS a list without * Only the listed origins may call the API from a browser page; a page on any other origin is refused by the browser. web.csp_frame_ancestors CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_FRAME_ANCESTORS a list without *, a bare scheme or a wildcard host Once CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_MODE=enforce, only the platform itself, the sites listed and, behind a registration token of the operator's own, the registered platforms may show its pages in an iframe: list a portal that embeds the platform before enforcing, or it is refused. web.public_widget_strict_rendering PUBLIC_WIDGET_STRICT_RENDERING true Public chat widget answers show only the images the platform serves (any other image becomes a link), open every link in a new tab, and drop inline styles, SVG, MathML and links other than http(s), mailto and tel. web.public_widget_uploads web_uploads_enabled on each agent, in Agents > the agent > Configuration > Web Exposure (Allow visitor uploads) false on every widget Visitors of the public chat widgets, who have no account, can only type: a widget that let them attach a document or an image to a message no longer offers it. The files already attached stay readable by the agent until the retention deletes them. Its value is how many live widgets allow uploads; see Visitor uploads on the public chat widget. integrations.oauth_token_url_strict OAUTH_TOKEN_URL_STRICT true Every OAuth token request (code exchange and refresh, for integrations and MCP servers) and every save of a token URL also refuses a token URL whose host is, or resolves to, a loopback, link-local, unspecified, reserved or multicast address, and any scheme but http(s); private networks stay allowed. An integration or MCP server whose token URL is on loopback stops exchanging and refreshing tokens until the URL points at another address of its identity provider or, on a development machine, its origin is listed in the loopback token URL origins. integrations.oauth_token_dev_trusted_origins OAUTH_TOKEN_DEV_TRUSTED_ORIGINS empty Under the strict OAuth token URL checks, every OAuth token request (code exchange and refresh, for integrations and MCP servers) refuses a token URL that resolves to a loopback address; only local development against an identity provider on the same machine needs the list. Without the strict checks the list has no effect. mcp.server_url_policy MCP_SERVER_URL_POLICY private_networks or public_only Saving a remote MCP server, and every connection the platform opens to one (redirects and OAuth discovery included), also refuses a URL whose host is, or resolves to, a loopback, link-local, unspecified, reserved or multicast address; public_only refuses private networks too. Cloud metadata addresses are refused in every mode. A server already saved at a refused address stops connecting until its URL changes, its origin is listed in the trusted MCP server origins, or it is reached through a relay group. mcp.server_trusted_origins MCP_SERVER_TRUSTED_ORIGINS empty Every remote MCP server is held to the MCP server URL policy; a listed origin is otherwise reached at any address but a cloud metadata one. agents.nova_llm_every_condition NOVA_LLM_MAX_CONDITIONS 0 While the Nova integration runs its full engine, every distinct llm: condition of the enabled rules is put to the model on each message it screens, one call per condition, as it always was. With a ceiling set, the conditions past it are not asked (those of block rules are kept first), and a rule resting on one cannot fire through that tier. assignments.webhook_require_secret WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_SECRET true A delivery to an assignment webhook with no secret configured is refused (401) instead of run: such an assignment stops triggering until it has a secret and the sender signs with it. tools.code_interpreter_disabled DISABLE_CODE_INTERPRETER true Agents and the General Assistant can no longer run Python in the code interpreter. tools.code_interpreter_extra_modules CODE_INTERPRETER_EXTRA_ALLOWED_MODULES empty The code interpreter keeps its whole module blocklist: code it runs cannot open network connections (it shares the host's network). tools.sandbox_command_declared_only CODE_INTERPRETER_COMMAND_ALLOW_ARGV false sandbox_run_command runs the checks a checked-out repository declares in .xtm-one/checks.toml and nothing else: an agent cannot run a command of its own in the sandbox container. The container has no network and no credential either way. tools.custom_tool_extra_modules CUSTOM_TOOL_EXTRA_ALLOWED_MODULES empty Python custom tools keep their whole module blocklist: in the subprocess fallback they cannot open network connections. tools.custom_tool_node_permission CUSTOM_TOOL_NODE_PERMISSION true A JavaScript custom tool run in the subprocess fallback gets no file system, child process, worker thread or native addon access (Node.js 24 or later); the network stays available. tools.custom_tool_sandbox CUSTOM_TOOL_SANDBOX docker or opensandbox Custom tools run in the hardened Docker container or an OpenSandbox container only: when that is unreachable they fail instead of falling back to a plain subprocess. tools.custom_tools_disabled DISABLE_CUSTOM_TOOLS true No custom tool (JavaScript or Python written by a user) runs anywhere: chat, assignments, flows and tests. tools.custom_variables_disabled DISABLE_CUSTOM_VARIABLES true The Variables feature is refused: its API and the agent builder's variable tools. tools.runner_result_bound RUNNER_MAX_RESULT_BYTES > 0 A runner file read never asks for more than the bound or 256 KiB, whichever is larger (text up to 256 KiB comes back inline, which the bound does not cap), and a larger file result is refused, so an agent cannot make a runner read a large file into memory. tools.runner_strict_path_confinement RUNNER_STRICT_PATH_CONFINEMENT true A restricted runner refuses a file command whose path leads outside its allowed folders through a symbolic link, junction or mount point, instead of running it with a warning (runners from this release or later). tools.svg_strict_rendering SVG_STRICT_RENDERING true An SVG a model is shown that declares an XML entity or references anything outside itself (a file path, a URL, another document) is not rendered at all, instead of being rendered with that reference dropped. Nothing is fetched or read from disk in either mode. tools.tool_call_budget_strict AGENT_LOOP_MAX_TOOL_CALLS_STRICT true A parallel batch of tool calls that crosses a run's budget runs only the calls that still fit; the others are answered "Not executed" instead of running. mcp.a2a_dev_trusted_origins A2A_CLIENT_DEV_TRUSTED_ORIGINS empty The A2A client reaches every partner over HTTPS at an address its destination guard accepts; only two deployments tested on one machine need the list. mcp.a2a_insecure_loopback A2A_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOOPBACK false A plain HTTP request from 127.0.0.1 or ::1 no longer counts as encrypted on the A2A surface. Behind a reverse proxy on the same host every partner request arrives from loopback, so the setting would waive HTTPS for all of them. mcp.client_id_metadata_documents MCP_CIMD_ENABLED false A client naming its own metadata document as its client_id (claude.ai, Claude Code, VS Code) is refused at /mcp/oauth/authorize and its tokens no longer refresh: it then needs dynamic registration or an API key. The platform no longer fetches client documents. mcp.dynamic_client_registration MCP_DCR_ENABLED false MCP clients can no longer register themselves (POST /mcp/oauth/register answers 403): an MCP client such as Claude Desktop or Cursor then needs an API key. Clients registered before keep working. mcp.outbound_dynamic_client_registration MCP_OUTBOUND_DCR_ENABLED false The platform no longer registers itself with a remote MCP server's authorization server: connecting an OAuth MCP server needs a client ID provisioned by hand. mcp.test_only_insecure_transport_peers TEST_ONLY_INSECURE_TRANSPORT_PEERS empty No network is exempted from the A2A HTTPS requirement: the list exists for the end-to-end test suite only. mcp.xtm_mcp_server xtm_mcp_enabled in Settings > MCP Endpoint false External MCP clients no longer reach this instance's own tools at /mcp/xtm: traces, the agent builder, knowledge search and skills, each within the caller's own rights. llm.trace_payloads trace_store_payloads, trace_storage_enabled in Settings > Observability (Store full payloads, Enable local trace storage) false, or trace storage off LLM traces no longer keep what was said: each call's prompts, answers, tool arguments and tool results are dropped, and an error message keeps its first 200 characters. Traces still show the timings, token counts, cost, model, tool names and status; with trace storage off, no trace is stored at all. It applies to the traces written from then on, on every server within seconds: traces stored before keep what they hold until the retention deletes them, and the Langfuse export, while it is on, still receives each call's payloads. infrastructure.debug_mode DEBUG false SQL statements are no longer echoed to the log with the tokens and encrypted values they carry, loopback no longer counts as HTTPS, password reset links are no longer written to the log when no SMTP server is set, and development-only tools are gone. infrastructure.quota_fail_mode QUOTA_FAIL_MODE closed While the quota store cannot be reached, agentic executions are refused instead of running unmetered; a due assignment run or background task is held until the store answers again. Always enforced in xtm_one mode, where quotas are part of the licence and it cannot be changed; configurable in copilot / dev mode. infrastructure.rate_limit_fail_mode RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_MODE closed While Redis cannot be reached, rate-limited requests (sign-in, password reset, webhooks, chat messages) are refused with a 503 instead of passing unthrottled.

The Enable local trace storage and Store full payloads switches of Observability are one control, llm.trace_payloads: it is enforced while either is off. By default traces keep their payloads, which the audit reports as information with the retention period; with payloads or storage off, it reports the pass.

The same report is available to scripts at GET /api/v1/security-audit, for administrators only. Every finding carries an id (for example infrastructure.debug_mode) that stays the same from one run to the next, so a script can follow a finding without relying on its title, which may include a count, and a finding about a control names it in control. controls lists every control that applies with its state, its value, default and hardened value and whether it is an opt_in, and controls_summary counts the controls per state.

docs.title: Security options
docs.text:
Security options holds the platform-wide security switches: trusted proxy headers (prefer FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS), canonical client addresses, HTTPS required for runner enrollment and MCP tokens (off by default: served and logged as before) and the IPv6 rate-limit prefix length, what rate limits and quotas do when their store cannot be read, the password length and the reset / invitation link lifetimes, the absolute session lifetime and the idle session timeout (see Session lifetime and idle timeout), MCP client registration, the strict OAuth token URL checks and the loopback token URL origins used in development under them, the A2A partner origins trusted in development and the loopback exemption used in tests, required webhook secrets, required verification of integration notifications (Slack, Microsoft Graph and LinkedIn deliveries the platform cannot verify - the Microsoft Graph notifications of the Teams bot's private and shared channels included, see Microsoft Teams - and the admin OAuth app's deliveries to other integrations: accepted as before and reported while it is off, refused when it is on), strict widget rendering, strict runner folder confinement, strict admin access for agent tools, the prompt guard switches (whether it refuses the General Assistant and widget messages its block rules match, whether it evaluates model answers, the tools whose results it screens and whether it withholds what a block rule matches), the code interpreter / custom tools / custom variables switches and the sandbox module and Node.js settings. Select Configure, change what you need and Save; the reset button next to a saved value returns it to its default. Every change is recorded in the audit log and applies on every server within a few seconds.

Tools screened by the prompt guard is empty by default: no tool result is screened. While a company-managed Nova integration is connected, the guard evaluates what a listed tool returns to an agent, the text of the files the result attaches included (images excluded), and records each rule match in the audit log as a Security alert (surface tool_result). The result reaches the agent as it is, and the evaluation runs beside the agent, which does not wait for it. With Withhold tool results a guard rule blocks on, a screened result that a block rule matches is withheld instead - the agent reads a short refusal naming the tool, without the result's files - and the agent waits for the guard's verdict on each screened result before it continues. In Configure, pick the tools from the list: built-in tools by name, integration and MCP tools by the name the platform gives them, custom tools by their id, shown under their current name - a custom tool stays screened when its owner renames it, with nothing to update here. A listed entry that no tool carries anymore (a deleted custom tool, a server that no longer offers the tool) is flagged so it can be removed.

Each option can also be set by an environment variable, and the variable wins: an option set that way shows an Env badge and "Set by environment variable X", and cannot be changed here until the variable is removed from the deployment. The full list, with the variables and defaults, is in Configuration.

In XTM One, Quotas when their store is unreachable is always closed: quotas are part of the licence, so agentic work is refused while their store cannot be reached. A due automation is held instead - shown as Held, charged once it runs, and run by itself once the store answers again (bounded by AI_UNAVAILABLE_HOLD_MAX_SECONDS). A store that refuses the platform's credentials (a wrong password, an ACL denial) is a configuration error, not an outage: that work is refused at once. The option shows a Read-only badge with that reason and cannot be changed, and its variable, QUOTA_FAIL_MODE, has no effect (set to open, the platform ignores it and logs a warning at startup).

The options are grouped under the categories of the security audit (Authentication, Sharing and access, Network, Browser security, Integrations, Agents, Assignments, Tools, MCP and A2A, Infrastructure): each under the category of the control it is.

Every option is also a security control, reported in the audit's Controls view with the value it resolves to (variable, saved value, then default), where that value comes from, and the Env or Read-only badge of a locked one. An option the security audit checks links to its finding: Security audit next to it opens the audit on that finding. The other way round, a finding whose recommendation names one of these options names the field and links to it: Configure <option> opens Security options on that field, ready to change. A finding whose option is set by its variable names only the variable and has no link, since the variable is what to change.

docs.title: Tool approvals
docs.text:
Tool approvals is the one place for the platform's side of tool approvals, which are opt-in. From the top:

  • Tool approvals: whether approvals are In use (an enabled agent or the General Assistant asks before running tools), Not in use or Suspended, with the agents that ask, each linking to its setting, and the Every agent asks by default switch that every agent left on Follow the platform default follows (the General Assistant included, where chat is available). A new install starts with it off; an upgrade keeps the value already stored, so an install that turned it on, or that an earlier release created with it on, keeps it on.
  • Tool rules: every tool this platform can name and whether it asks first, with Let it run without asking, Make it ask first and Back to the default per tool, Add a tool by name for one not connected yet, and Make all its reads ask first per connected platform. The rules can be prepared before anything asks; the card says they change nothing until then.
  • Approval for connected platforms: per connected platform, whether its tools ask while it cannot show a prompt.
  • Suspend all approvals: the emergency switch that lets every tool call run without asking, for everyone, until approvals are resumed.

Each change asks for confirmation and is recorded in the audit log. Each agent's own setting is under the agent's Configuration > Tooling, and each person's own approvals under Profile > Tool approvals. See Human approval of tool calls for what asks first and why.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication controls sign-in and identity behavior:

  • local authentication rules
  • registration policy
  • OpenID Connect
  • SAML 2.0
  • SAML group mapping
  • allowed email domains

See Authentication for every setting.

docs.title: Secret vaults
docs.text: Secret vaults connects your enterprise secret managers, so that a secret field (of an integration, an MCP server, a variable, an LLM provider...) stores a reference to a secret kept in your vault instead of its value. See Secret vaults.

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
API keys lists every personal API key of the platform, whoever owns it: its owner (and whether that account is deactivated), its prefix, what it reaches (Full access, or its surfaces, Read-only and its agents), its expiry, its own limits, its request count, its last use and when it was created. The key itself is never shown: it is stored hashed and only its owner saw it, once, when it was created. See API Keys tab for what each setting means.

Filter by status (All, Active, Expired, Revoked), by exposure (No expiry, Full access, Beyond the maximum lifetime, the keys of active accounts the security audit reports), by owner (one or several users) and by key name, prefix or owner name. The status, exposure and owner filters are kept in the address (/settings/security/api-keys?status=active&issue=no_expiry&owner=<user id>), so you can link to them.

Revoke stops a key at once, on every surface, and notifies its owner in the notification bell. A revoked key stays listed as revoked; its owner can delete it but not reactivate it. The key provisioned by ADMIN_TOKEN cannot be revoked here: unset the variable to remove it. Revoking is recorded in the audit log, like creating, changing and deleting a key.

A user's own keys are also on the API Keys tab of their page in Users, with the same Revoke.

Scripts use GET /api/v1/admin/api-keys (with status, issue, search, owner_id - repeat it for several owners -, limit and offset; with_summary=true adds totals over every matching key, not only the page) and POST /api/v1/admin/api-keys/{id}/revoke.

docs.title: Emergency stop
docs.text: Emergency stop holds the emergency stop API token: generate, rotate or revoke the token that presses the emergency stop from outside a session, and print the emergency procedure to keep on paper. The token is shown once; the card then shows only its prefix, who generated it, and when it was last used.

docs.title: Memory purge
docs.text: Memory purge permanently deletes every agent memory on the platform, for example after discovering a flaw in the memory system. The purge cannot be undone and is recorded in the audit log.

docs.title: Storage & retention
docs.text:
Settings > Usage and quotas > Storage & retention (administrators) lists every category of stored file with how long it is kept, from when the days count, how many files and how much space it holds today, how many were deleted, and what the last hourly sweep deleted.

Category Holds Default Agent working files scratch files assistants write while they work 60 days after the last use Agent deliverables files assistants hand to people to download 60 days after the last use Other agent files files tools and MCP servers return Never Chat uploads files people attach in a conversation Never Channel files files received from Teams, Outlook and the other channels Never Check pictures frames and captures a tool makes for the assistant to look at 7 days after creation

A use is a download, a preview, a read by an assistant or an attach; it starts the days again. A file an open work item, a workset, an active shared state, a presentation, a report or a video still uses is never deleted. A deleted file keeps its row: the chat, the files panel, run attachments and the Files page show a muted card with when and why, its download answers 410 Gone, and an assistant reading it is told the file was deleted.

Edit turns each value into a field (days; 0 = never). A value shorter than the current one deletes files at the next sweep, so Save waits for Preview, which counts per category the files and the space the next sweep would delete and how many it keeps because they are in use. Every change is recorded in the audit log with its old and new values. A category whose environment variable is set (FILE_RETENTION_*_DAYS, AGENT_CHECK_FILE_RETENTION_DAYS, see configuration) is shown locked with the variable's name.

The same values are read and written through GET / PUT /api/v1/settings/file-retention, POST /api/v1/settings/file-retention/preview, and read by any signed-in caller through GET /api/v1/settings/file-retention/rules.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
Observability covers tracing, model costs and usage reporting. It holds three cards.

The observability setup, edited with Configure:

  • Enable local trace storage: whether LLM traces are stored at all. Traces are kept in PostgreSQL, or in ClickHouse when the deployment configures one (see Configuration); the card says which, and whether the store answers.
  • Store full payloads: whether a trace keeps what was said (prompts, answers, tool arguments and tool results) or only its timings, token counts, cost, model, tool names and status
  • Trace retention (days): how long stored traces are kept
  • Audit log retention (days): how long audit log entries are kept, 90 days by default, from 30 to 3650 days. An hourly job deletes the older entries in batches, and keeps each user's most recent sign-in so their last login stays known. See Logs.

  • Coordination retention: how long the coordination records are kept, each from 0 to 3650 days, 0 keeping them forever:

    • Closed work items (days): done and cancelled work items are deleted this many days after their last update, 90 by default (WORK_ITEM_RESOLVED_RETENTION_DAYS).
    • Resolved shared state (days): resolved shared state entries are deleted this many days after their last update, 90 by default (SHARED_STATE_RESOLVED_RETENTION_DAYS).
    • Unclaimed open work items (days): open work items nobody picks up are cancelled this many days after their last activity, 14 by default (WORK_ITEM_ABANDONED_AFTER_DAYS).
    • Archived shared state items (days): list items moved to an archive entry are dropped this many days after they were archived, 14 by default (SHARED_STATE_ARCHIVE_RETENTION_DAYS).
    • Resolved worksets (days): resolved worksets are deleted with their documents, 7 days by default (WORKSET_RESOLVED_RETENTION_DAYS).
    • Runs (days): finished runs of Operations > Executions (completed, failed, skipped or cancelled) are deleted with their files this many days after they ended, 90 by default (ASSIGNMENT_RUN_RETENTION_DAYS). A run still working, queued or waiting for a person is never deleted, nor one that holds a work item claim or a shared state lease, has a background task still running, or is the parent of a run that is kept. The assignments' execution counts do not change. Each pass that deletes runs writes one audit log entry with the count and the window.
    • Discarded CTEM signals (days): signals the scope gate discarded are deleted this many days after they were last seen, 30 by default (CTEM_SIGNAL_DISCARDED_RETENTION_DAYS).
    • Watchlist CTEM signals (days): watchlist signals are deleted this many days after they were last seen, 90 by default (CTEM_SIGNAL_WATCHLIST_RETENTION_DAYS).
    • Unmatched CTEM signals (days): signals not in your inventory are deleted this many days after they were last seen, 30 by default (CTEM_SIGNAL_UNMATCHED_RETENTION_DAYS). After an inventory change only the ones seen within this window are decided again; an older one is decided again at its next sighting.

    A CTEM signal a person dismissed or linked to a case is never deleted, and a deleted signal seen again comes back as a new signal.

    The environment variables give the defaults; a value saved here wins. An hourly sweep deletes what is past each window in batches and keeps draining on every scheduler tick until nothing is left. Active shared state entries and work items still open are never deleted. The values are read and written with coordination_retention in GET / PUT /api/v1/settings/observability, and get_platform_overview reports work_item_retention_days, shared_state_retention_days and run_retention_days. - Langfuse configuration, the optional export to Langfuse, which the two switches above do not govern

A change to the two switches applies within a few seconds on every server, to the traces written from then on; traces already stored keep what they hold until the retention deletes them. See What a trace keeps. The card also warns when the daily cost aggregation has not run for more than 48 hours, when prices have not been updated for a while, and lists the models seen in traces that have no price.

Model Pricing holds the price of each model, which gives traces their cost:

  • Sync detected seed loads the prices from the seed file the platform ships with; Import JSON file loads them from a file of yours. A price you edited by hand is kept: the result counts it as Custom skipped.
  • Manage model prices opens the price table, where you search, add and edit rows by provider and model (a model can be matched by a pattern).
  • Reprice $0 traces gives a cost to the traces recorded at $0 because their model had no price at the time, and recomputes the daily totals. With Only from the price's effective date, only traces recorded after the price took effect are repriced.

Departments maps people to your organization's departments, so that usage and cost can be reported per department. See Departments.

Model Pricing and Departments stay editable while AI is turned off.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
Quality defines the feedback criteria: what people score when they rate an agent's work, on top of the thumbs up or down. Once a criterion exists, the rating dialog asks for it after either thumb, and each score can be skipped.

A criterion has a kind, fixed once it is created:

  • Scale: a whole step between two bounds, such as 1 to 5
  • Categorical: one of a few options, each worth a score from 0 to 1 (a warm tone can be worth 1 and a cold one 0)
  • Numeric: any number between a minimum and a maximum

Each criterion also has a weight. A rating's weighted score is the weighted mean of its scores, each read on a common 0 to 1 scale; a rating with no score is worth its thumb (1 for up, 0 for down), and so is every rating while no criterion exists. A weight of 0 keeps a criterion visible without counting it, but the enabled criteria cannot all weigh 0.

Switch a criterion off to stop asking for it while keeping the scores already given. Deleting it also deletes every score given on it. The agent's Feedback tab shows, per criterion, how many scores it received, their average, their distribution, and the daily average over the last 30 days.

docs.title: What regular users should know
docs.text:
If you are not an administrator, you may only see AI Models and Channels & Bots, or even fewer options depending on deployment. AI Models and the model pickers list only the providers and models you may use.

That does not mean your account is broken. It only means shared configuration is intentionally restricted.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: The AI Catalog page explains where you can browse published resources and add them to your account.

docs.title: Users and groups
docs.text: Users and Groups, in the administration menu, are where administrators manage accounts and the groups that share resources, set limits and decide AI access. Both pages are for administrators only.

docs.title: The Users page
docs.text:
Users lists every account with its role, a Platform Admin or Disabled badge where it applies, and how many integrations, MCP servers, agents and knowledge bases it owns. Search by name or email, or filter by group.

Open a user to see their page. Its tabs are:

  • Profile: name, email, role, status, sign-in method, two-factor authentication and password.
  • Groups: the groups the user belongs to.
  • Objects: the agents, knowledge bases, MCP servers, custom tools and integrations the user owns.
  • API Keys: the user's personal API keys, with Revoke (see API keys).
  • Quotas: the user's own limits and their usage.
  • Activity: the audit log entries of the user's actions, with a search box and Action and Entity filters.

docs.title: Add a user
docs.text:
There are two ways to give someone an account.

New User creates the account at once. Choose the Account Type:

  • Local Account: you set the email, the full name and a password, and pass the password on to the person.
  • SSO Pre-provision: the account is created without a password. The first time the person signs in through single sign-on, the account is linked to them by email, with the role and profile you set. This type needs single sign-on to be turned on first.

Turn on Administrator to make the account an administrator.

Invite user emails the person a single-use link to create their own account, with the email address and the role you set. The link works once and expires after 7 days by default (see Admin-managed accounts). An invitation needs the platform to send email: without a mail server configured, the invitation is refused with an error that says so (see Password reset and email).

The same dialog lists the Pending invitations, with their role and expiry. Revoke one to cancel it, for example to send it again: an email address can have only one pending invitation, and an address that already has an account cannot be invited.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
An account is either an administrator or a user. Promote and Demote, at the top of the user's page, switch the role. The change applies on the person's next request.

The bootstrap administrator, the account set by ADMIN_EMAIL in the deployment, carries the Platform Admin badge. It cannot be demoted, disabled or deleted, its email cannot be changed nor given to another account, and every restart makes it an administrator again (see Local accounts).

When the platform has no account yet, the first account registered becomes an administrator.

docs.title: Disable, enable or delete an account
docs.text:
Disable stops the person from signing in and keeps everything they own. While the account is disabled, the assignments and flows it owns are paused, shared ones included; the company-managed ones it created keep running. What was shared with the person stays shared, so Enable gives them back the access they had.

Delete removes the account for good and cannot be undone:

  • the company-managed resources the person owned (agents, assignments, integrations, knowledge bases, MCP servers, custom tools, channel bots, prompts, variables) are handed to you, so they keep working for everyone;
  • their private resources are deleted with the account: agents, assignments and their runs, integrations, knowledge bases, MCP servers, custom tools, conversations, API keys and the rest;
  • their access to resources shared with them is removed, and their memory is cleared;
  • the audit log entries of their own actions go with the account. The entry of the deletion, written under your name, stays.

You cannot disable or delete your own account. Prefer Disable when you may need the account or its history again.

docs.title: Email address
docs.text:
People cannot change their own email address: the other Filigran platforms (OpenCTI, OpenAEV, OpenCRQ) find a person's account by it. The Email card of the user's page changes it, for local and SSO accounts alike, to an address no other account has and, when Allowed Domains is set, in one of those domains. The change applies at once:

  • when the platform sends email, the old and the new address are both told of the change, without a link;
  • password reset links already sent to the old address stop working;
  • the audit log records the old and the new address.

docs.title: Passwords
docs.text:
The Password card of the user's page offers two ways to change a local password:

  • Email a reset link sends the person a single-use link to choose their own password: you never see it. The link expires after 24 hours by default. It needs the platform to send email: without a mail server, the request is refused with an error.
  • Set a password directly sets the password you type, which you then pass on to the person. It works without email.

For an account that signs in only through single sign-on, neither is available: the identity provider manages the password. For an account that has both, the change only affects its local password; single sign-on is unaffected.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
The Two-factor authentication card shows whether the person has enrolled an authenticator app, and when. Nobody can read their secret or recovery codes, administrators included.

If the person has lost their device and their recovery codes, Reset two-factor removes the enrollment: they sign in with their password alone until they enroll a new device, and their old authenticator and recovery codes stop working at once. Only the person can turn two-factor authentication on, from their own profile. Each reset is recorded in the audit log. See Two-factor authentication.

docs.title: Impersonate a user
docs.text:
Impersonate lets you use the platform as the person sees it, to reproduce a problem they report. It is offered for an active account other than your own, and not while you are already impersonating someone.

While you impersonate, a banner at the top of every page names the person and you, with Stop Impersonating to return to your own account. The impersonation ends when your own session ends.

What to know before you start:

  • Starting an impersonation is recorded in the audit log. What you then do is done as the person, and is recorded under their name.
  • Some actions are refused while you impersonate: creating, changing or deleting an API key, signing in to another product through XTM One, and signing in XTM One Desktop.
  • You have the person's access, not yours: what they cannot see, you cannot see either.

docs.title: Quotas for one user
docs.text:
The Quotas tab sets limits for this person alone, above their groups' limits and the platform default. For agentic executions (chat messages and assignment runs), set a limit per period, turn on Unlimited to lift it, or clear it to inherit from the person's groups or the platform. The platform-wide quota still applies as a hard cap, and a limit cannot exceed what the license allows.

The tab also shows the person's current usage. Reset usage sets their counters back to zero, and is recorded in the audit log. See Quotas for how the limits combine.

Quotas need an activated license or a registered Enterprise Edition platform.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
Groups lists every group with its member count. New Group creates one with a name and an optional description.

Groups have two uses:

  • Sharing. A resource shared with a group is shared with its current members. Adding someone to the group gives them access; removing them takes it away.
  • Settings for a team. A group can carry quotas and an AI switch, and can be reserved an LLM provider or kept off one (see Reserving a provider for teams and Keeping people off a provider).

With SAML, groups can also be created and filled from the identity provider at every sign-in (see Group mapping). A group with Auto join on takes in everyone who signs in through single sign-on.

A group's page has four tabs:

  • Overview: its name, description and Kind, with the AI access and Auto join cards. The kind (Org unit, Access list, Distribution list, or Not classified) tells LLM Analytics which groups are org units.
  • Members: add members with Add Member, remove them, and search or filter by role. From a user's page, the Groups tab does the same with Add to Group.
  • Managers: the people who follow the AI usage of the group's members. See Group managers.
  • Quotas: the limit each member gets. A user's own quota wins over the group's; with no group limit, members inherit the platform default.

Deleting a group removes its members' access to what was shared with the group. A group that an LLM provider excludes cannot be deleted: remove it from the provider's exclusions in Settings > AI Models first.

docs.title: Group managers
