Both semantics: and llm: numbers are refused on save (REST and the rules tab) unless they are between 0 and 1, which is what the Nova engine accepts.

Synced community rules always arrive with action = log; an administrator switches a rule to block on the Nova rules tab, and that decision survives every sync (nova_rule_sync never resets action or enabled). A rule whose upstream update is refused on sync (a syntax error, a number outside 0-1) keeps its last version that parsed, with its action, instead of being removed, and a sync that could not read one of the repository's files removes no rule; the rule source line on the tab names the rules kept and the files not read.

docs.title: Agentic quota
docs.text:
One agentic execution — a chat turn, an assignment run, a background sub-agent task, a flow's agent step, a browser-extension task — spends one agentic action from the user's action quota. The action is deducted before the agent runs, which is what lets the platform refuse a request instead of discovering mid-run that it was never allowed. The consequence is that a run which ends in failure has already spent an action, on work the user never received.

The agent failure pool gives that unit back, up to a bounded number of failures per agent:

Variable Required Default Description AGENT_FAILURE_QUOTA_REFUND_ENABLED No true Master switch for the failure pool. On by default — spending an action on a run the platform failed to deliver is the wrong default, and the pool is what keeps that from becoming free unlimited retries. Set it to false to deduct an action for every failure, like a success. AGENT_FAILURE_QUOTA_POOL No 5 Failures credited back per agent, per user, per pool window. The N+1th failure in the same window spends its action normally. 0 closes the pool without touching the switch above.

How it behaves:

  • The first AGENT_FAILURE_QUOTA_POOL failed runs of a given agent, for a given user, in the current window have their action credited back. Every failure after that spends an action like a successful run — so a provider outage or a broken tool is forgiven, while an agent that fails every time keeps consuming the action quota.
  • The window is one year, on the anniversary of your Filigran license. With no license installed it falls back to the anniversary of this platform instance, and if neither is readable, to the calendar year. Settings → Quotas shows which anchor is in use and the exact renewal date.
  • It is scoped per agent and per user: on a company-managed agent shared by a whole company, one user's failures never spend another user's pool.
  • Failed runs still count as work performed: the execution telemetry and the run's own record are untouched, and the run is still visible as failed. Only the action is credited back.
  • A user whose agentic quota is unlimited is never pooled. When no tier caps the user — the license quotas are at infinity or there is no platform_limit, the platform default is Unlimited, and neither the user nor their groups carry a limit — a failed run costs them nothing, so no pool slot is spent and nothing is credited back from the pool. Their agents can therefore never "exhaust" a pool, and Settings → Quotas shows their rows as Not applicable. Users and groups with a limit of their own are pooled exactly as above; the free credit-back below is unchanged either way.

docs.title: When no model was ever called
docs.text:
A run that could not call a model at all — the provider was unreachable, it was down or overloaded, this platform is not configured / authorised to call it, or the platform abandoned the run itself (the worker was lost, its lease expired, its deadline blew mid-run) — is a different case: nothing was produced, and nothing on the user's side caused it. Those runs have their action credited back for free, outside the pool: they never consume a pool slot, and they are never refused, however many of them happen. One provider outage must not be able to exhaust an agent's whole allowance and leave real failures charged for the rest of the year.

The free credit-back is not gated by AGENT_FAILURE_QUOTA_REFUND_ENABLED: that variable sizes the pool, and an unreachable provider is not a pool question. Turning the pool off still credits back a run that never reached a model.

What counts as "never reached a model" (is_provider_unavailable_error in app/llm/router.py, the single source of truth shared by chat, assignment runs and extension tasks):

Failure Credited back Paid by No LLM provider configured at all Yes Free Connection error, DNS failure, timeout Yes Free Provider 5xx / 529 overload, gateway 502-504 Yes Free Every provider in the failover chain failed for one of the above Yes Free Run abandoned by the orchestration engine (worker lost, lease expired, deadline blown mid-run) Yes Free Background sub-agent task abandoned the same way Yes Free Rate limit / 429 Yes The agent's pool Invalid API key, provider not authorised (401/403) Yes The agent's pool Provider account out of credit (insufficient_quota, billing) Yes The agent's pool Context overflow, request too large (413) Yes The agent's pool Tool error, malformed model output, any other crash Yes The agent's pool

Everything the provider replies sits on the pool side deliberately — a rate limit, a rejected credential, an account out of credit. They are persistent and indefinitely reproducible: forgiving them without a bound would stop the action quota metering entirely for as long as they last, which is the free-unlimited-retries outcome the pool exists to prevent. They are still forgiven — out of the bounded pool, which is what bounded is for.

Settings → Quotas reports the two reasons apart — "credited back · agent failure" (from the pools) and "credited back · provider unavailable" (free) — with a per-agent breakdown, so a large number can be attributed before anyone acts on it.

A run the engine abandons is failed from a different process than the one that charged it, so the credit-back cannot rely on anything held in memory: the charge is recorded on the run itself when it happens, and the abandonment path reads it back. A run that was never claimed — nobody ever executed it, which is what a scheduled run does when no worker is running — was never charged, so there is nothing to credit and nothing appears.

Background sub-agent tasks are covered too, by a different mechanism: their action is charged inside the agent turn, where nothing knows about the task, so the charge writes a short-lived metering receipt keyed by the task and the engine's attempt. The abandonment path redeems that receipt — atomically, so two sweeps cannot credit twice — which means it credits back only what was really charged rather than assuming a charge happened.

A run the engine re-runs after losing its worker (a restart, or a database outage long enough for the worker's lease to lapse) is charged one action in total. Each charge belongs to the attempt that made it: the re-run credits back what the lost attempt was charged, for free, and is charged its own. The lost attempt may still be running — losing the lease does not stop it — but it can no longer credit that charge a second time, and if it only reaches its own charge after the re-run started, that charge is given straight back.

Not yet covered

Flow runs still are not. A flow can meter several actions (one per agent node), so a single receipt per run does not describe it; the mechanism extends — one receipt per step — but the abandonment path has to enumerate the steps it charged. A worker lost mid-flow therefore still leaves those actions charged.

Bounded on the generous side

A run whose first model calls succeeded and which then died on a provider outage is also credited back for free — charging a user for an outage they could not see is the worse error. Removing that approximation needs failures to carry a classifiable cause instead of the free-text error string they carry today.

  • The General Assistant is not covered — there is no agent to pool against.
  • Resetting a user's quota usage from the admin UI also restores their pools.

docs.title: Recharging a pool before its renewal date
docs.text:
An administrator can restore every pool on the platform without waiting for the anniversary, by redeeming a support code issued by Filigran in Settings → Quotas → Agent Failure Pool.

  • A code is a single signed token (XTMP-…) that the admin pastes in. It is verified offline, against the same Filigran trust anchor the platform already uses for license certificates — an air-gapped deployment can redeem one, and no secret is added to the platform.
  • Each code carries an expiry and an identifier, and is single-use: the identifier is recorded in support_code_redemptions on redemption, so a second attempt (or a code shared between two admins) is refused. Settings → Quotas lists the codes already redeemed, when, and by whom.
  • A code is normally bound to one PLATFORM_ID and refused elsewhere; Filigran can also issue a global code, redeemable on any platform.
  • Because verification is offline, a code cannot be revoked once issued — it can only expire. Ask support for a short validity when that matters.

Refusals are shown inline with the reason: not signed by Filigran, altered, expired on a date, issued for another platform, or already used on a date.

docs.title: Resetting the platform-wide usage counters
docs.text:
The same support-code mechanism can reset the platform-wide usage counters the license ceilings are enforced against (platform_quota_reset codes, redeemed from the license banner in Settings → Quotas), for instance when a proof of concept used the license's allowance before the evaluation ended.

  • The reset clears the current day, month and year windows of the agentic and sandbox counters by default, in Redis and in quota_global_usage alike; the code can narrow the windows or include the LLM proxy counter. Past windows, per-user usage and the ceilings themselves are left as they are.
  • It is single-use, offline-verified and platform-bound exactly like a pool recharge, and audited.
  • Issuing side: backend/scripts/mint_support_code.py --kind platform_quota_reset [--quota-types …] [--periods …].

Why a pool instead of refunding every failure

Nothing available at the point of failure reliably separates "the provider was down" from "this prompt can never succeed". Crediting back every failure would make an endlessly retried, hopeless run free; crediting none spends a user's action quota on outages they did not cause. A small pool per agent covers the accidental case and charges the systematic one to the quota, with no classification to get wrong.

Sizing is environment-only

Both variables are environment-only, by design: what consumes the action quota belongs to whoever operates the deployment, not to whoever administers the tenant. Changing either one requires a restart. The admin screen is read-only apart from redeeming a support code.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Variable Required Default Description LOG_LEVEL No info debug, info, warning, error, critical. LOG_FORMAT No json json (structured) or console (human-readable). When unset, defaults to json in production or console when DEBUG=true.

docs.title: Email (SMTP)
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description SMTP_HOSTNAME No — SMTP server hostname. SMTP_PORT No 587 SMTP port. SMTP_USERNAME No — SMTP authentication username. SMTP_PASSWORD No — SMTP authentication password. SMTP_FROM No SMTP_USERNAME Sender address for outgoing emails. SMTP_FROM_NAME No Filigran Copilot Sender display name. Set it to your platform name (XTM One in .env.sample). SMTP_STARTTLS No true Connect in plain text, then upgrade with STARTTLS (port 587). SMTP_USE_TLS No false Encrypt from the first byte (implicit TLS, port 465). Wins over SMTP_STARTTLS when both are set. MODEL_ANNOUNCEMENT_EMAILS_DISABLED No false Turn every model announcement email off for the whole platform: the emails sent when a deployment changes its env-managed catalog (MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_ENABLED) and the ones an administrator sends from Settings > AI Models alike. A boot with it on closes the announcements still queued without sending them, a process with it on sends none, and Settings no longer offers to email the users (the test email included). Model changes are still recorded: once it is off again, a boot with MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_ENABLED and SMTP sends the latest env change skipped meanwhile, under the same conditions as below. MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_ENABLED No false Email the platform's users when a boot (or switching AI on) finds the env-managed model catalog changed: DEFAULT_MODEL moved, an LLM_PROVIDER_<P>_MODELS list gained or lost a model, or a capability the environment pins (DEFAULT_IMAGE_*, DEFAULT_VIDEO_*, DEFAULT_SPEECH_*, DEFAULT_MUSIC_*, DEFAULT_DECISION_*) became available or moved to another model. One email per change names the new default model, the models now available, the ones retired, and each capability with what it does and its model ("Video generation is now available", "New AI capabilities in your platform" when several arrive at once). A capability the environment stops pinning is not announced, and on the first boot of a release that tracks capabilities, those the platform already had are not announced as new. The video and music models are announced only while the Video Studio is on (ENABLED_FEATURES=VIDEO_STUDIO), the one feature that uses them; turning it on announces them. While it is off, the speech model is announced for reading answers aloud only, with no word of the Video Studio. Needs SMTP. Whether a change goes out is decided by the boot that records it, from its own configuration, so a pod still running the previous environment during a rolling deploy cannot drop it: a change recorded while this is off (or without SMTP) is sent by a later boot that has both, within 7 days, as long as nobody was emailed about it and it still describes the live catalog. What became of each change (queued, skipped and why, sent to how many) is logged at WARNING. A change waits until the env catalog has stayed unchanged for MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_SETTLE_MINUTES, so the changes of successive deploys reach the users as one email. Emails go out in English from the scheduler, a batch per minute, oldest change first, never twice to the same person: an email whose delivery could not be confirmed (the connection dropped mid-send, a worker stopped) is not retried. Announcements an administrator sends from Settings > AI Models do not depend on this switch, only on MODEL_ANNOUNCEMENT_EMAILS_DISABLED (see Emailing users about model changes). MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_RECIPIENTS No all all (every active user) or admins, for the changes a boot finds. Announcements sent from Settings go to every active user. The bootstrap ADMIN_EMAIL account is never emailed. MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_BATCH_SIZE No 20 Emails sent per scheduler tick (one a minute); the rest follows on the next ticks. Keep it under your mail server's sending limit: a hosted mailbox allowing 200 emails an hour needs 3 or less. MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_SETTLE_MINUTES No 30 How long, in minutes (0 to 1440), the env-managed model catalog must stay unchanged before the change a boot found is emailed. Every env change deployed before then (a corrected rollout, a second release, a rolling restart with new values) is added to the same email and restarts the wait, and a change reverted meanwhile is never sent. 0 sends from the next scheduler tick. Announcements sent from Settings are never held. MODEL_CATALOG_CHANGES_WINDOW_HOURS No 24 How far back, in hours (1 to 168), the model list saves an administrator has not emailed yet are combined into the model changes Settings > AI Models offers to email. Every save is kept; a model added then retired within the window (or the reverse) cancels out, and a change the live catalog no longer holds is left out.

Without SMTP_HOSTNAME, the platform sends no email. An administrator's invitation email or password-reset email is refused with an error (an invitation can still be created without email, and its link copied); a user's own Forgot password request sends nothing, and writes the link to the log only with DEBUG=true.

Every email the platform sends (password reset, invitation, model announcements) follows the Filigran email layout and loads its images from <FRONTEND_URL>/email-assets/: the recipients' mail client must reach FRONTEND_URL to show the logos.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Variable Required Default Description LANGFUSE_HOST No https://cloud.langfuse.com Langfuse server URL. LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY No — Langfuse public key. LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY No — Langfuse secret key. PROMETHEUS_ENABLED No false Enable Prometheus metrics endpoint. PROMETHEUS_BEARER_TOKEN No — Bearer token for metrics endpoint (min 16 chars). TRACING_STORE_PROVIDER No postgres Where LLM traces are kept: postgres (the platform database) or clickhouse. With clickhouse, traces are written to both stores and read from ClickHouse. See Request tracing. CLICKHOUSE_HOST, CLICKHOUSE_PORT No localhost, 8123 ClickHouse HTTP address. CLICKHOUSE_USERNAME, CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD No default, — ClickHouse credentials. CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE No default ClickHouse database the trace tables are created in. CLICKHOUSE_SECURE No false HTTPS to ClickHouse. CLICKHOUSE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS No 5 Seconds allowed to connect to ClickHouse.

docs.title: Usage telemetry
docs.text:
What is sent, where and how often: Usage telemetry.

Variable Required Default Description TELEMETRY_ENABLED No true Anonymous usage telemetry to Filigran. false turns it off: the platform makes no connection to the collector, not even the startup check. Read at startup. TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT No Filigran's collector (its staging one with DEBUG=true or PLATFORM_MODE=dev) OTLP/HTTP endpoint (.../v1/metrics) the metrics are sent to, your own collector for example. TELEMETRY_TAGS No — Comma-separated deployment tags (saas,eu-west) sent with every metric. Trimmed, lowercased, deduplicated and sorted before they are sent.

docs.title: Security feature flags
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description AGENT_TOOLS_STRICT_ADMIN_ACCESS No false Keep every agent tool of an admin - the agent builder, the agent trace inspection and the work-items delegation, in chat and on the XTM One MCP server - to the admin's own, group-shared and company-managed objects, like every other caller: the agents, assignments, runs, traces, evaluations, knowledge bases, skills and other entities a tool looks up, lists or binds. The admin role still counts where a tool checks a permission (a company-managed object, an admin-only setting). By default an admin's agent reaches everything, as the admin does in the UI and through the REST API; the Security Audit reports the default while an agent carries one of these tools, chat is on (the General Assistant offers the agent builder in every conversation) or the XTM One MCP server is enabled. Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. DISABLE_CODE_INTERPRETER No true (xtm_one mode) Disable code interpreter at infra level. Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. DISABLE_CUSTOM_TOOLS No true (xtm_one mode) Disable custom tools at infra level. Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. CUSTOM_TOOL_SANDBOX No auto Custom tool execution mode: auto, docker, subprocess, opensandbox. opensandbox delegates to an OpenSandbox-managed container (also used by the code interpreter) and requires the OpenSandbox connection variables below. PLATFORM_HEALTH_SPEND_LIMITS_UNLOCKED No false Platform Health spends outside the agentic quota, bounded only by its own spend ceilings (Budget, Analysis and Module Analyst in Settings > Platform Health). Unset or false: those ceilings stay at their built-in defaults, shown locked, and a change to them is refused; a stored value is kept, not applied. true: the stored values apply and the ceilings are editable. Restart required to take effect. DISABLE_SANDBOX_QUOTA_USAGE No false Opt out of per-user sandbox usage counting (quota_usage rows with usage_type="sandbox", alongside the existing LLM-proxy/agentic usage). Counted by default; set true for self-hosted/on-prem deployments that manage their own sandbox infrastructure independently of hosted usage-based billing. Restart required to take effect. INTEGRATION_NOTIFICATIONS_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION No false Refuse every Slack event on /api/v1/integrations/notifications/slack and every Microsoft Graph change notification the platform cannot authenticate, those of the Teams bot's private and shared channels on /api/channels/teams/graph-notifications included. By default a Slack integration with no usable signing secret keeps receiving its events without a verified signature, and a Graph subscription recorded without a clientState keeps working, each with a warning in the log and a Security Audit finding. A delivery that a stored Slack signing secret or a Graph clientState does not prove never reaches what that secret or clientState protects, whatever the setting. The same setting limits what the admin OAuth app's webhook (/api/hooks/providers/<provider>) and the LinkedIn notification URL deliver to the admin app's integrations the agent owner may use (for a GitHub App event, those recording its installation or, recording none, whose own token sees it), and drops a LinkedIn notification when no LinkedIn client secret is configured; by default they reach what they reached before, with a warning and a Security Audit finding. That webhook accepts, without a check, a delivery for a provider whose OAuth default holds no webhook secret, and by default one for a provider with no OAuth default (with the setting on, such a provider reaches nothing); both are reported the same way. For the Teams bot's private and shared channels, a notification that does not carry the subscription id and the random secret (clientState) XTM One recorded for its channel is still acted on by default whenever earlier releases acted on it, with a warning and a Security Audit finding, and the subscriptions created before 2026-07-02 (whose secret anyone who knows the team id can compute) are kept and renewed; with the setting on, such a notification is refused, the maintenance pass replaces those subscriptions and the ones whose secret can no longer be decrypted (if Microsoft Graph refuses to create a replacement, that channel's follow-ups stop until a later pass creates it), and what a refused notification held back is read back from Microsoft Graph, up to four hours back. Nothing to set on upgrade. See Real-time Slack, Microsoft Graph or LinkedIn events do not arrive and Microsoft Teams. Also in Settings > Access and security (Require verified integration notifications); the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. WORK_ITEM_NOTIFY_TEST_RECIPIENTS No empty The targets, comma-separated, a test work item may name for its end notification: an address (payload.notify.user), a Teams chat id (payload.notify.chat_id) or team_id/channel_id (a Teams channel). A test work item is one whose correlation key starts with retest: or test:, or whose title starts with Notify retest. Any other recipient is refused when the item is created or updated, so a platform retest never messages a real person. The sending account's own chat (chat_id 48:notes) is always allowed. Empty: a test item may only notify that own chat. WORK_ITEM_DEPLOYMENT_REPOSITORIES No XTM-One-Platform/xtm-one The repositories (owner/name, comma-separated) whose deployments the platform observes. A work item may wait on the deployment of a change (blocked_on_refs kind deployment) only in one of them, since such a wait is released when a running build carries the merge. A deployment wait on any other repository is refused when the item is saved, with the alternatives: a workflow_run wait on that repository's release workflow, or a reason with a start date for the re-check. WORK_ITEM_STALE_REF_WAIT_DAYS No 7 How many days a blocked work item waiting on pull requests, issues, deployments or workflow runs may stay quiet before it is shown as stale ("needs a look"). An item whose start date is ahead is never stale on inactivity, and one waiting on a deployment the platform does not observe always is. 0 treats such a wait like any blocked item (the 24 h window). PROMPT_GUARD_SCANNED_TOOLS No empty The tools whose results the connected prompt guard screens, comma-separated: a tool's registered name for a built-in, integration or MCP tool (for example web_fetch,search_jira_issues), and custom:<id> for a custom tool, with the custom tool's id - it stays screened when its owner renames it. While a company-managed Nova integration is connected, the guard evaluates what a listed tool returns to an agent - the text the agent reads, followed by the text of the files the result attaches (images excluded) - and records each rule match in the audit log (Security alert, surface tool_result, with the tool, the rules and their action). The result itself is left exactly as it is, and the evaluation runs beside the agent, which does not wait for it. Empty by default: no tool result is screened, and an agent run does what it did before the setting existed. Also in Settings > Access and security (Tools screened by the prompt guard), where the tools are picked from a list; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_TOOL_RESULTS No false With PROMPT_GUARD_SCANNED_TOOLS set, withhold a screened tool result that a block rule matches: the agent reads a short refusal naming the tool instead, without the files the result carried, and the result is not reused for an identical call. The agent then waits for the guard's verdict on each screened result before it continues (at most 20 seconds each, the results of one parallel batch evaluated together, four at a time in each platform or worker process); a guard that fails or runs out of time lets the result through. Off, a match is recorded and the result reaches the agent as it is; the security audit reports that log-only mode while a guard is connected. Also in Settings > Access and security (Withhold tool results a guard rule blocks); the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PUBLIC_WIDGET_STRICT_RENDERING No false Public chat widget: show only the images the platform serves in an answer (any other image becomes a link the visitor can open, so the visitor's browser never fetches a URL an answer chose), open every link of an answer in a new tab, and render answers without inline styles, presentational markup (align, bgcolor, <font>, ...), SVG or MathML, with links of the http, https, mailto and tel schemes only. By default answers render as they always did: an image from any http(s) host is shown, an HTML link without a target opens in the page, and inline styles, presentational markup, SVG / MathML drawings and links of any other scheme (msteams:, sms:, ...) are kept. Script is removed in both modes: script elements, event handlers, javascript: / vbscript: / data: URLs, frames, forms and embedded objects. Links that launch a Windows program with a public exploitation history (ms-msdt:, search-ms:, ms-officecmd:, ms-appinstaller:, ...) are removed in both modes too, their text kept, as they are in the Office add-in; app links (slack:, msteams:, ...) and the Office document links (ms-word:, ms-excel:, ...) keep working. The security audit (Settings → Security) reports the default while a widget is enabled. Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PUBLIC_WIDGET_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS No 7 Public chat widget visitor uploads (see Visitor uploads on the public chat widget): the files a visitor attached are deleted once their conversation has had no message for this many days; a file uploaded and never sent with a message is deleted after a day, and the files of a deleted conversation within the hour. A value below 1 is read as 1: the retention cannot be switched off. SVG_STRICT_RENDERING No false SVGs a model is shown (a chat upload, a user-message image, a tool result such as an agent reading back the diagram it drew): refuse, instead of rendering, an SVG that declares an XML entity or references anything outside itself - a file path, an http(s) URL or another document, in an <image>, <feImage> or <use> or a url(...) in an attribute. By default such an SVG renders with that reference dropped - what resvg drew there on its own, as it follows only references inside the document - and an internal entity (an Adobe Illustrator export declares its namespaces this way) is expanded within a bound. Nothing is fetched or read from disk in either mode, and a nested SVG embedded as a data: URI (draw.io icons) is checked under the same rules. The security audit (Settings → Security) reports the default. PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_GENERAL_ASSISTANT No false While a prompt guard (the Nova integration) is connected, a General Assistant message is evaluated before the model is called and every rule match is written to the audit log (security_alert, source: nova_guard, surface: chat_message, chat_surface: general_assistant). By default the message is answered even when a block rule matched (the entry records rule_action: block, action: allowed): the General Assistant was not guarded before, so nothing it answers today is refused on upgrade. Set true to refuse such a message with the guard's message, as agent chat always does. The security audit reports which of the two applies while a guard is connected. Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_PUBLIC_WIDGET No false The same for a public chat widget visitor's message (chat_surface: public_widget). A visitor has no account, so the entry is written as the guard (system:nova_guard) and attached to the admin account the widget acts as (ADMIN_EMAIL). With true, a refused message reaches no model and its agentic action is given back. PROMPT_GUARD_MODEL_OUTPUT No off Evaluate the model's answer with the connected prompt guard (the Nova integration): off, log or block. Covered: the final answer of every top-level agent turn (web chat, the REST chat API, channel bots, the chat embedded in OpenCTI / OpenAEV, A2A, the MCP agent endpoints, the LLM proxy, the browser extension, background tasks, flows), the General Assistant's (a transfer's included) and the public widget's. Not covered: a consult's or a transfer's inner answer (its parent's answer is), evaluation runs, the OpenAEV autonomous run's cycles after the first, and assignment runs, whose result reaches their owner and which act on the outside world through write tools. off evaluates nothing. log returns every answer unchanged and at once, and evaluates it in the background (at most 4 at a time per process and 64 pending, 20 seconds each, the first 20,000 characters); a match is written to the audit log (security_alert, surface: model_output, action: allowed). block evaluates an answer before it is delivered and replaces one a block rule matches with a withheld notice (action: block), where the answer is delivered whole: the REST chat API, channel bots, A2A, the MCP endpoints, the LLM proxy, the browser extension, background tasks, the widget's non-streaming endpoint and a transfer from the General Assistant. A streamed answer (web chat, the streaming chat embedded in OpenCTI / OpenAEV, the widget's stream) has already been shown when it is complete, so in block it is evaluated and audited after delivery as in log, with streamed: true, and never withheld. An evaluation that fails or runs out of time delivers the answer. With no guard connected nothing is evaluated whatever the value. Write-tool arguments (an email body, a ticket comment) are not evaluated. The security audit reports the value while a guard is connected. Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field.

Embedding the chat widget on a site with its own Content-Security-Policy

The widget (/api/v1/public/widget.js) runs inside the page of the site that embeds it, in a Shadow DOM, so that site's Content-Security-Policy applies to everything it loads. If the site sends one, it must allow:

  • script-src: the XTM One origin (the widget script);
  • connect-src: the XTM One origin (the API calls and the streamed answers);
  • img-src: the XTM One origin (the widget logo and the images the platform serves), plus the hosts answers link images from - by default an answer can show an image from any http(s) host, and with PUBLIC_WIDGET_STRICT_RENDERING=true it shows only the platform's own;
  • style-src: 'unsafe-inline' and https://fonts.googleapis.com;
  • font-src: https://fonts.gstatic.com.

'unsafe-inline' in style-src is the only choice today: the widget styles itself with a <style> element it builds at run time and with an inline style attribute in its markup, and it supports no nonce. A hash cannot replace it either: the stylesheet changes with every widget release, and a hash does not cover a style attribute without 'unsafe-hashes'. Without it the widget's styles are blocked and it renders unstyled.

In both rendering modes, an image the platform stores for the visitor's session - a file or a generated image an answer shows by its platform address (/api/v1/chat/files/<id>, /api/v1/chat/images/<id>) - is shown inline and loads from the XTM One origin through the visitor's own session (/api/v1/public/chat/<token>/sessions/<session>/...): the visitor needs no platform account, and the platform refuses any file or image the session does not own.

docs.title: Visitor uploads on the public chat widget
docs.text:
A widget visitor has no account (see Publish an agent on a website). Each agent's widget can let its visitors attach files to their messages: Allow visitor uploads in the agent's Configuration > Channels > Web Exposure, off for every widget until its owner turns it on. The security audit reports the widgets that allow it (control web.public_widget_uploads, a warning while one does). With it on, the widget shows an attach button and takes a pasted screenshot or a dropped file. The agent receives each file as in the web chat - a document as its text (the first 50,000 characters, what the chat upload message carries), an image by its pixels, and every file's id for the tools that take a file - but a document never reaches the model as its native bytes, even with a provider that reads PDF or Office files natively: the model reads exactly the text the prompt guard evaluated. What bounds an anonymous uploader:

  • Types: PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx, .xls), PowerPoint (.pptx), text and data files (.txt, .md, .csv, .tsv, .json, .jsonl, .ndjson, .xml, .yaml, .yml, .log, .html, .htm) and raster images (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp), decided on the file name and checked against the file's content: an image is decoded as the format its name says and may declare at most 20,000 pixels a side and 50 million in all, an Office document must be an Office package whose parts and expanded size are bounded (no archive under another name). The type the browser declares is ignored. No SVG, archive, audio or video.
  • Size and load: the chat upload limit, 40 MB a file. A larger body is refused on its declared length before it is read, and cut off past the limit when it declares none. Each platform process reads at most 4 visitor files at once, uploads and the documents of messages being sent alike; past that a visitor is told to retry (503 with Retry-After), and a message refused this way keeps its files in the widget. Every image and Office file is decoded, and every document read, when it is uploaded, in a worker process of its own, never on the threads the platform's own document work uses: a file that takes more than 30 seconds, or more than 2 GB of address space where the operating system lets that cap be set (Linux), is stopped and refused (422). A visitor who disconnects mid-upload still counts against those 4 files until the store ends, and leaves no stored file that the quotas and the retention do not count - unless the object store and the database both fail at that moment, in which case the object's key is written to the error log for an operator to remove.
  • Budgets: 20 uploads an hour per client address and 200 an hour per widget across all its visitors. Both refuse while Redis cannot be reached, whatever RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_MODE says.
  • Storage: 10 files and 100 MB per conversation, 2 GB per widget across its conversations, checked before the body is read and again when the file is written.
  • Content: while a prompt guard (the Nova integration) is connected, the text the model will read of each document is evaluated before the file is stored, and a match is written to the audit log (security_alert, surface: widget_upload, as the guard, attached to the admin account the widget acts as). With PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_PUBLIC_WIDGET=true, a file a block rule matches is refused.
  • Reach: a visitor's file belongs to its conversation and to no user. Only the visitor's own session downloads it (an image inline, every other file as a download, never kept by a cache); on the platform only administrators can open it.
  • Retention: deleted once the conversation has had no message for PUBLIC_WIDGET_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS (7 by default), a file never sent with a message after a day, and the files of a deleted conversation within the hour - the stored object first, then its record, so an object store that does not answer leaves both for the next hourly pass. Turning the switch off stops new uploads; the files already attached follow the same retention.

Every refused upload says why - its type, its size, a budget, the conversation's or the widget's storage, the content check - and the widget shows the reason next to the file.

docs.title: Settings > Access and security options
docs.text:
These security options are set in Settings > Access and security by an administrator, or by their environment variable. The rule is the one the AI Models defaults and the Langfuse card follow: the variable, when set (and not blank), wins - the field is then shown read-only with the variable's name ("Set by environment variable X") and a change to it is refused. With the variable unset, the value saved in Settings > Access and security applies; with nothing saved, the default below applies, which is the platform's behaviour before the options reached the UI. A change made on one replica applies on every web and worker process within 5 seconds.

One option is fixed in xtm_one mode (and ai_disabled): quotas are part of the Filigran licence, so Quotas when their store is unreachable is always closed - while the quota store cannot be reached, agentic work is refused rather than run unmetered, requests with no account behind them included (anonymous channel users, the public chat widget, the platform MCP key). A due automation (a scheduled, webhook or integration-event assignment run, a background task) is not refused but held: it is shown as Held, is charged once it runs, and runs by itself once the store answers again, bounded by AI_UNAVAILABLE_HOLD_MAX_SECONDS. A store that refuses the platform's credentials (a wrong password, an ACL denial) is a configuration error, not an outage: that work is refused at once. The field is shown read-only with that reason and a change to it is refused; QUOTA_FAIL_MODE has no effect (set to open, it is ignored with a warning at startup), and a value already saved in Settings > Access and security is kept but not applied. In copilot / dev mode the option follows the rule above.

docs.title: XTM Hub registration
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description XTM_HUB_DEFAULT_URL No https://hub.filigran.io The XTM Hub this platform registers with by default, like OpenCTI's XTM__XTMHUB_URL and OpenAEV's OPENAEV_XTM_HUB_URL. It is the XTM Hub URL proposed in Settings > Parameters, the one automatic registration uses, the XTM Hub the product switcher and the home dashboard link to, and the address of an XTM Hub integration that names none. An absolute http(s) URL without credentials, query or fragment; anything else refuses to start. A registration token is only sent to it over https, or to an XTM Hub on this machine.

An XTM One instance deployed in an XTM Platform trial is registered with the XTM Hub automatically: once it is up, the deployer calls PUT /api/v1/xtm-hub/registration/auto with an administrator API key (Authorization: Bearer, for example the ADMIN_TOKEN key) and the body {"token": "<platform token>"}, the token the XTM Hub issued for this instance. XTM One then registers itself with XTM_HUB_DEFAULT_URL under its PLATFORM_ID, which must be the instance ID the XTM Hub knows for this deployment. The call answers 204 once the XTM Hub accepted the registration, 400 when the token is not an XTM Hub platform token, and 502 when the XTM Hub refused it or could not be reached; nothing is stored then. The registration is then checked every hour like one made from Settings.

docs.title: XTM Hub sign-in gate
docs.text:
Restricts sign-in to people XTM Hub has entitled to this XTM One instance, and lets the Hub decide who is an administrator here. OIDC only — XTM Hub does not provide SAML.

Variable Required Default Description XTM_HUB_ADMIN_GROUP No — The role, in this instance's XTM Hub claim, that means administrator. Matched exactly, including case. Setting it enables the gate; empty leaves OIDC behaving exactly as it does without this feature.

The gate reads a claim named after this instance — {PLATFORM_ID}_groups — so PLATFORM_ID must be set when you enable it. It is the switch that is XTM_HUB_ADMIN_GROUP rather than PLATFORM_ID, because forcing a platform identifier is an ordinary thing to do for clone/restore identity continuity and must not enable a sign-in gate as a side effect. Enabling the gate without PLATFORM_ID refuses to start, rather than silently refusing every sign-in.

Enabling it changes three things at once:

  • Every sign-in is checked, not only the first. Someone who already has an account and has since lost their Hub entitlement is turned away too.
  • A refused sign-in creates no account and lands on the login page with a neutral message. The reason is in the server log, not on the page — the person is unauthenticated, and the criteria describe how your IdP is configured.
  • Administrator follows the Hub in both directions: granted when the Hub asserts it, and removed when it stops. The account named by ADMIN_EMAIL is exempt from removal, so a Hub-side group change cannot lock you out of your own instance.

If a misconfigured gate refuses everyone, sign in with a local account — that route stays available and is the way back in.

docs.title: MCP OAuth
docs.text:
MCP OAuth runs in two independent directions, and each has its own switch.

Inbound — an external MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, …) connecting to XTM One. The platform acts as the authorization server and lets clients self-register, which the MCP specification requires because a client has no credentials before any user session exists.

Outbound — XTM One connecting to a remote MCP server. With no client ID configured, the platform discovers the remote authorization server and registers itself, so a server can be added from its URL alone. This is the MCP specification's intended onboarding path: modern remote MCP servers do not issue static credentials to paste into a form.

Variable Required Default Description MCP_DCR_ENABLED No true Inbound. Allow external MCP clients to self-register against this platform (POST /mcp/oauth/register, RFC 7591). The endpoint is unauthenticated by specification, so it is protected by a per-IP rate limit and a bounded client table rather than a login. Set false to turn registration off entirely (the endpoint then returns 403). A confidential client receives its client_secret in the answer, so under CREDENTIAL_TRANSPORT_STRICT a registration the platform cannot confirm arrived over HTTPS is refused first (400 {"error": "invalid_client_metadata", "error_description": "https required"}). Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. MCP_DCR_MAX_CLIENTS No 500 Inbound. Upper bound on dynamically registered clients. At the cap the oldest registrations are evicted; RFC 7591 clients re-register transparently. Values below 1 are clamped to 1. MCP_DCR_RATE_LIMIT No 5 Inbound. Registrations per hour from one client IP at POST /mcp/oauth/register. A hosted client (claude.ai, ChatGPT) registers one client per fresh connection, always from its provider's addresses: raise it when many people connect from such a client and it does not use a client metadata document. Values below 1 are clamped to 1. MCP_CIMD_ENABLED No true Inbound. Accept OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents (MCP 2025-11-25): a client names its own HTTPS metadata document as its client_id instead of registering, which is what claude.ai, Claude Code and VS Code use when the platform advertises it (client_id_metadata_document_supported). The platform fetches the document from a public address only (the outbound URL policy, connecting to the address it checked), with no redirect, within 5 seconds and 16 KiB in all, at most 20 fetches per client IP, 10 per host and 60 for the whole platform per minute (refused while Redis is unavailable), and caches it for its Cache-Control max-age (5 minutes to 1 hour, 1 hour by default); a known client is served from its cached entry for up to 24 hours more when a refetch cannot be made. Why a document was refused is logged, not shown to the caller. Only public clients with a client_name whose redirect URIs are HTTPS or loopback are accepted, and a person still signs in and consents on a page naming the client by its host. The refresh tokens of one authorization stop after 90 days, and sooner once its document is refused. Set false to refuse them: such a client then needs dynamic registration or an API key, and its tokens stop refreshing. Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. MCP_OUTBOUND_DCR_ENABLED No true Outbound. Let the platform register itself with a remote MCP server that advertises a registration endpoint, so remote servers can be connected without pre-provisioned credentials. Set false to require every outbound OAuth client to be provisioned by hand — connecting a remote server then needs an explicitly configured client ID. Also in Settings > Access and security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field.

docs.title: Code interpreter sandbox workspace
docs.text:
Every conversation and assignment run has a durable directory, workspace/, that the code interpreter keeps between calls (see Working in the sandbox workspace). Its files are stored in the platform bucket (S3_BUCKET) under sandbox-workspaces/<workspace id>/, one object per distinct content, and its manifest in PostgreSQL; the sandbox receives only its own workspace's files and never a storage credential. No volume is needed: every replica and worker reads the same workspaces.

Variable Required Default Description CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_ENABLED No true Keep a workspace per conversation and run, offer session=true, to_workspace_path and the sandbox_* / materialize_repository tools. false brings back the stateless code interpreter of earlier releases (no workspace, no tool or argument added). CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_QUOTA_MB No 2048 Size limit of one workspace, in MiB. A call that would go past it saves nothing it wrote under workspace/ and says so. CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_MAX_FILES No 20000 Files one workspace may hold. CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_IDLE_TTL_HOURS No 168 A workspace unused for this long is deleted by the hourly sweep. Archiving or deleting a conversation deletes its workspace at once. CODE_INTERPRETER_RUN_WORKSPACE_IDLE_TTL_HOURS No 24 An assignment run's workspace is deleted as soon as the run ends (completed, failed, skipped or cancelled). One whose run has not ended is deleted after this long unused, unless the run waits on a person (then CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_IDLE_TTL_HOURS applies). CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_MANIFEST_ENTRIES No 40 Files the code_interpreter description and the resume note list; the rest are counted. CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_CACHE_MB No 2048 Local sandbox only: what each backend process keeps of the workspace contents it downloaded, under the system temporary directory, least recently used first out. 0 disables the cache (every call downloads what it mounts). CODE_INTERPRETER_KERNEL_IDLE_SECONDS No 900 A session=true kernel unused for this long stops (minimum 30). On OpenSandbox it is also the kernel container's lifetime, renewed by every call. CODE_INTERPRETER_KERNEL_MAX_PER_PROCESS No 8 Local sandbox only: kernels one backend process keeps, the least recently used stopped first. CODE_INTERPRETER_COMMAND_MAX_SECONDS No 1800 OpenSandbox only: the longest a check run by sandbox_run_command may take; a check's own timeout in .xtm-one/checks.toml is capped by it. The command's container is discarded after a timeout. CODE_INTERPRETER_COMMAND_ALLOW_ARGV No false OpenSandbox only: let sandbox_run_command run an argv the checkout did not declare in .xtm-one/checks.toml. Off: only declared checks run, and a refusal lists them. The container has no network and no credential either way. CODE_INTERPRETER_PACKAGE_ALLOWLIST No empty Packages code_interpreter(packages=[...]) may install into a workspace, comma-separated distribution names. Empty: installs are off and the argument is not offered. The server installs wheels only, checked against the index's sha256, and runs no install script; a package the sandboxed code imports can import modules the sandbox blocks to the code itself, so list only packages you trust. The security audit reports a non-empty list. CODE_INTERPRETER_PACKAGE_INDEX_URL No PyPI The package index installs read: a PEP 691 or PEP 503 "simple" index, such as a PyPI mirror or proxy.

Storage sizing. Plan for the bucket to hold, at most, the active conversations times the quota; in practice a workspace holds what an agent downloaded or wrote (a repository subset is usually a few MB), and an unused one goes after CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_IDLE_TTL_HOURS. An assignment run's workspace goes when the run ends; after an upgrade, the first hourly sweeps delete the workspaces of the runs that ended before it (reason run_ended in the sweep's log line, with the bytes freed). Prometheus reports the total (xtmone_sandbox_workspaces{measure="bytes"}, see Monitoring), and the get_platform_overview tool reports sandbox_workspaces (count, bytes, by holder, the top owners and what the clean-up freed) next to files.storage_bytes. With the local sandbox, give each backend pod's temporary directory room for CODE_INTERPRETER_WORKSPACE_CACHE_MB plus the files of the calls running at once.

docs.title: OpenSandbox
docs.text:
Only used when CUSTOM_TOOL_SANDBOX=opensandbox. Governs the OpenSandbox-managed sandbox used by the code interpreter and by custom tools.

Variable Required Default Description OPENSANDBOX_DOMAIN Yes (if opensandbox mode) localhost:8090 Host (and optional port) of the OpenSandbox service. docker-compose.yml and the dev override docker-compose.dev.yml default it to the opensandbox service (opensandbox:8090). The default isn't enforced at startup — a production deployment that forgets to set this won't fail loudly, it will just try to reach localhost:8090 and fail to connect. OPENSANDBOX_PROTOCOL No http Protocol used to reach OpenSandbox (http or https). OPENSANDBOX_API_KEY Yes (with the opensandbox service) — API key for authenticating to OpenSandbox. docker-compose.yml gives the same value to the opensandbox service as its own key: unset, that server (v0.2.1 and later) refuses to start. The dev override docker-compose.dev.yml defaults it to copilot-dev-opensandbox on both sides. OPENSANDBOX_IMAGES No python:sandbox-python:0.4,nodejs:sandbox-nodejs:0.4 Per-key container image, as comma-separated key:image pairs (split on the first : per entry, so a registry:port-qualified image survives intact). Overrides merge on top of the defaults, so overriding one key leaves the other on its default. OPENSANDBOX_K8S_POOL_NAMES No — (cold start, k8s-only) Per-key Kubernetes Pool binding, as comma-separated key:pool-name pairs, e.g. python:my-python-pool,nodejs:my-js-pool. A Pool's warm pods run one fixed image, so one name can't back both sandbox kinds — a key missing from the mapping (or the whole variable unset) cold-starts for that key. OPENSANDBOX_K8S_NAMESPACE No — (reaper off, k8s-only) The namespace the OpenSandbox server creates its sandboxes and Pool pods in. Set, the worker reaps it every minute, and at once after a pooled create timed out: it deletes the Pool pods that ended (Failed, Succeeded, Evicted) or stayed not Running and ready past OPENSANDBOX_POOL_STUCK_SECONDS, which a Pool counts toward its warm buffer and never replaces, and the BatchSandbox objects past their expireTime. The platform's service account needs pods and batchsandboxes.sandbox.opensandbox.io get, list and delete in that namespace; without them, or outside a cluster, the reaper logs one line and does nothing. Deleted objects are counted by xtmone_sandbox_pool_reaped_total{kind, reason}. OPENSANDBOX_POOL_STUCK_SECONDS No 600 How long a Pool pod may stay Pending, Unknown or Running but not ready before the reaper deletes it (minimum 60). Keep it above the server's sandbox_create_timeout_seconds. OPENSANDBOX_NETWORK_ALLOW No — (all egress denied) Comma-separated list of domains/IPs to allow as egress from every OpenSandbox container. Empty means all egress is denied. In a JavaScript custom tool, a fetch to a host outside the list is refused at once with the egress-policy message, and a fetch to a listed host fails after 10 s when the host does not accept the connection. CODE_INTERPRETER_OPEN_EGRESS No false Outbound internet for the OpenSandbox code interpreter only (one-shot runs and the session kernel): its container gets a default-allow egress policy that still denies the cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal), the cluster's internal names (*.svc, *.cluster.local, *.internal, *.local) and every loopback, private, CGNAT and link-local range, and socket, http, urllib, requests, httpx and aiohttp become importable; the escape modules stay blocked. Outbound only: no credential is ever put in the sandbox. The local code interpreter shares the backend's network and is never opened. A deployment network policy on the code interpreter's Pool stays the packet-level floor and must let it out too. false turns it back off. SANDBOX_REGISTRY_MIRROR_URL No — (off) URL of a read-only npm, PyPI and Maven Central mirror proxy for the containers sandbox_run_command and sandbox_start_service create (never the code interpreter or a custom tool), e.g. http://registry-mirror:8080. Set, its host is added to their egress allow-list and npm, Yarn, corepack, pip and uv install through it (/npm/ and /pypi/simple/ routes), and Maven through /maven/ (a settings file mirroring every repository, mirrorOf *, named by MAVEN_ARGS). The shipped proxy is backend/sandbox/registry-mirror/nginx.conf: GET and HEAD only, no credential forwarded, any other path refused. Keep registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org and repo.maven.apache.org out of OPENSANDBOX_NETWORK_ALLOW so the mirror is the only route. A URL with a user, a password, a query or a fragment is refused at startup. Empty: the dev images install offline from the caches they bake. SANDBOX_CPU No 1 CPU requested for each OpenSandbox container (code interpreter + custom tools). Passed through as-is to the OpenSandbox SDK's resource argument on the cold-start path. When OPENSANDBOX_K8S_POOL_NAMES binds that sandbox kind to a k8s Pool, it does not size the container — the Pool manifest's own resources.requests governs warm-pod sizing instead, so there's no sync requirement between the two - see dev-docs/opensandbox-pool-management.md. It also sets OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS in every OpenSandbox container to this value rounded up to a whole CPU (at least 1), so numerical libraries such as numpy start one thread per allocated CPU, not one per host core. SANDBOX_RAM No 128Mi Memory requested for each OpenSandbox container. Same cold-start-only pass-through as SANDBOX_CPU. Both take a bare value for every image key or a per-key list in the OPENSANDBOX_IMAGES convention (128Mi,python-dev:2Gi: the entry without a key is the default), so the dev images of sandbox_run_command (python-dev, nodejs-dev, built by backend/sandbox/build-dev-image.sh with the repository's locked dependencies) can be sized for a test suite without resizing every sandbox. The code interpreter and the custom Python tools read the python key, the custom JavaScript tools the nodejs key. OPENSANDBOX_USE_SERVER_PROXY No false Route sandbox traffic through the OpenSandbox server instead of connecting directly to each sandbox's endpoint. Useful for any deployment topology where this process can reach the OpenSandbox server but not the individual sandbox endpoints it hands back — e.g. a process on the host against a containerized server, which advertises endpoints via a hostname like host.docker.internal that only resolves from inside containers, or a production/k8s deployment where sandbox pods aren't directly routable from this process but the server's service is.

docs.title: Running the OpenSandbox server itself
docs.text:
The variables above configure how the platform connects to an OpenSandbox server. These configure how that server itself runs:

Variable Required Default Description CONTAINER_ENGINE_SOCKET No /var/run/docker.sock Container engine API socket mounted into the opensandbox service, which starts the sandbox containers through it. Under rootless Podman, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock (enable podman.socket). The service runs with SELinux labeling disabled (security_opt: label=disable), which an SELinux host needs for it to use the socket, and which leaves it unconfined by SELinux there; it has no effect on a host without SELinux.

docker-compose.yml defines the OpenSandbox server, the opensandbox service, under the opensandbox profile: it starts only when you enable that profile (docker compose --profile opensandbox up -d, or COMPOSE_PROFILES=opensandbox in .env), and then needs OPENSANDBOX_API_KEY. It runs the sandboxes as Docker containers on the same host and answers at opensandbox:8090: set CUSTOM_TOOL_SANDBOX=opensandbox in .env. The platform and the workers read CUSTOM_TOOL_SANDBOX and the OPENSANDBOX_* connection variables from .env, and OPENSANDBOX_DOMAIN defaults to opensandbox:8090. The server advertises each sandbox as host.docker.internal:<port> (backend/sandbox/sandbox.docker.toml); the platform and worker services map that name to the host (extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway), so they connect to the sandboxes directly and OPENSANDBOX_USE_SERVER_PROXY stays false. The dev override docker-compose.dev.yml always starts it. To run the sandboxes as pods on a Kubernetes cluster instead, point OPENSANDBOX_DOMAIN at an opensandbox-server deployed on that cluster; the cluster needs the BatchSandbox CRD, opensandbox-controller and the kata-fc RuntimeClass (see dev-docs/opensandbox-pool-management.md).

  • Target namespace on Kubernetes: set via the namespace key in [kubernetes] of the server's configuration file (backend/sandbox/sandbox.k8s.firecracker.toml is a starting point) — there's no env var for this specific setting, it's TOML-only. (opensandbox-server itself does read two env vars: OPENSANDBOX_SERVER_API_KEY for its API key, and SANDBOX_CONFIG_PATH as a fallback for --config when no CLI flag is given — but neither substitutes for TOML settings like namespace.) Defaults to null (server default) if omitted. See the OpenSandbox server configuration reference for the full [kubernetes] section.

docs.title: Sandbox call log fields
docs.text:
Every OpenSandbox-routed call (code interpreter, custom JS tool, custom Python tool) emits one structured sandbox_call log event to stdout (JSON in production — see Logging above), independent of the quota_usage counters. These fields are stable across releases so a log pipeline (e.g. shipping stdout into Grafana/Loki) can filter and aggregate on them; a field not listed here (e.g. level, timestamp, logger) is generic structlog metadata, not part of this schema.

Field Type Present when Description usage_type string Always One of code_interpreter, custom_tool_js, custom_tool_python. user_id string (UUID) Only when the call had a known user context The caller's user ID. outcome string Always success or failure. failure_reason string Only when outcome=failure One of sandbox_ready_timeout (the sandbox never became ready in time), sandbox_create_failed (other sandbox-creation error), sandbox_create_error (unexpected error creating the sandbox), nonzero_exit (the executed code/tool exited with a non-zero status), execution_error (an unexpected error while running the code/tool). cpu_used_percentage float Successful calls and nonzero_exit failures, when metrics could be retrieved CPU used, as a percentage. cpu_count float Same as cpu_used_percentage Number of CPU cores allocated to the sandbox. memory_used_in_mib float Same as cpu_used_percentage Memory used, in MiB. memory_total_in_mib float Same as cpu_used_percentage Memory allocated to the sandbox, in MiB. tte_ms integer Successful calls and nonzero_exit failures, when the sandbox backend reported a completed execution Time-to-execute: the sandbox's own reported execution duration, in milliseconds (not overall call time, which also includes sandbox creation/setup). Can be absent even on a nonzero_exit failure if the process errored before an execution-complete event was ever emitted (e.g. an immediate crash). egress_default_action string Always Always "deny" today. egress_allow_list array of strings Always (may be empty) The egress allow-list (OPENSANDBOX_NETWORK_ALLOW) applied when the sandbox was created.

CPU/RAM/TTE are omitted (not emitted as null) whenever they aren't available — e.g. no sandbox was ever created (sandbox_ready_timeout, sandbox_create_failed, sandbox_create_error), or the metrics lookup itself failed or timed out. A slow or unreachable metrics lookup is bounded to a few seconds and never delays or fails the underlying sandbox call.

docs.title: Webhook delivery
docs.text:
Governs POST /api/hooks/assignments/{assignment_id} — the endpoint an external system (SIEM/SOAR, ticketing, CI) posts to in order to drive an agent.

A delivery that finds its assignment busy is queued, not discarded: it becomes a run in the queued status, and an accepted delivery produces exactly one run, eventually. Queued runs start the moment they are queued and whenever a run ends, up to ASSIGNMENT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS runs of one assignment at once, in turns across agents and assignments so one busy assignment cannot starve the others. Runs that must not overlap - the same ticket, the same thread - are kept one at a time by an assignment's ordering_key (below). Schedules, manual triggers and follow-ups keep their own overlap guard: they never start beside an active run.

Variable Required Default Description ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_ENABLED No true Per-assignment webhook (POST /api/hooks/assignments/{id}) only: queue its deliveries that arrive while the assignment is busy. Integration events follow INTEGRATION_EVENT_QUEUE_ENABLED instead. Set false only to restore the legacy behaviour, where such a delivery was discarded and still answered 200. INTEGRATION_EVENT_QUEUE_ENABLED No false Pushed integration events - a Slack event, a Microsoft Graph or LinkedIn notification, a provider or agent webhook - that arrive while every slot of their assignment is taken. false: the overlap guard skips them, as it always did (a Slack message is still fetched by the poller). true: they are queued, past the queue cap with a warning if need be, and start as slots free. Polled events (email, Teams and Slack messages) are always queued, whatever this says - see below. ASSIGNMENT_EVENT_DEDUP_WINDOW_SECONDS No 600 One run per inbound event on an agent. A second event-triggered run with the same dedup key (a mail's Message-ID, a calendar event and its modification instant, a provider event id) on the same agent within this many seconds is recorded as a skipped run (skipped: duplicate of run <id>, counted in the assignment's filtered events) instead of starting, across the agent's assignments and across delivery paths (a Graph notification and the poll behind it, two mailboxes the mail reached, a delegated pick-up naming the Message-ID). The same window covers an agent account of the same agent on a mailbox the mail reached: whichever of the assignment and the agent account takes the mail first answers it, the other leaves it (the assignment run is recorded as skipped: duplicate of run the agent account <id>, the agent account's activity as already_handled). An assignment's trigger_config.dedup_window_seconds overrides it; 0 turns the dedup off for it. Scheduled runs are not affected. MAIL_SEND_GUARD_WINDOW_SECONDS No 300 One answer per conversation from a mailbox an agent sends through, the last line behind the dedup above. Before a Microsoft mail tool sends (send_microsoft_email, send_microsoft_draft, a reply draft sent, reply_microsoft_email_in_thread with send=true), it takes a short lock on the conversation for the sending mailbox and looks for a message that mailbox (any agent, any run) already sent in that conversation within this many seconds: its own record of the last send, then the mailbox's Sent Items. Found, the send is refused and the tool answer names the earlier message (when it was sent, its subject, its recipients, its id and link); the agent can pass force_duplicate=true when a second message is really wanted. A message from someone else that arrived in the conversation after the earlier send lets the new send go out (it answers that message); an automatic reply (an out-of-office answer, told by its Auto-Submitted / X-Autoreply / Precedence: auto_reply headers or its "Automatic reply:" subject) does not. A new email's conversation is its subject (reply and forward prefixes dropped) and its To / Cc addresses. 0 turns the guard off. INTEGRATION_EVENT_GRAPH_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED No true Deliver Microsoft integration-event assignments (new email, Teams messages, replies and chat messages, calendar changes, email flag changes) through Microsoft Graph change notifications posted to BASE_URL/api/v1/integrations/notifications/microsoft, within seconds instead of on the 5-minute poll. Only effective when BASE_URL is a public https URL (not localhost, a private address or a .local / .internal / .lan host). The scheduler creates each subscription with a random clientState, renews it before it expires and deletes it when the assignment no longer needs it; an assignment whose subscription cannot be created, or lapses, is polled as before, and picks up from the last notified event. false deletes the subscriptions on the next pass and polls everything. ASSIGNMENT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS No 10 Runs of one assignment started from its queue at once (webhook deliveries, polled and pushed integration events), clamped to 1-50. An assignment's trigger_config.max_concurrent_runs overrides it. To keep up, the cap must exceed deliveries per second times the seconds a run holds its slot: 30 deliveries a minute of 6-22 s runs keep 8 in flight on average. 1 restores one run at a time. ASSIGNMENT_DISPATCH_MAX_PENDING_RUNS No 0 Queued runs promoted and still waiting for a worker, across the platform. The drain stops there, so a promoted run starts within a reconciler cycle and one busy assignment cannot fill the worker pool ahead of the others. 0 = MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS. ASSIGNMENT_FAIR_SHARE_ENABLED No true Share the worker pool between fleets when a free slot claims the next run: a delegated sub-agent run whose parent is still running goes first, then one run per fleet in turn (an agent outside any fleet counts as its own fleet), oldest first within a fleet. A storm of one fleet's events then delays another fleet's scheduled or event run by one slot release at most. false restores the strict oldest-first claim. ASSIGNMENT_FLEET_MAX_SHARE No 0.5 The share of the pool (MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS times the workers) one fleet may hold while another fleet has runs waiting; past it, its runs go after the others'. Nothing is refused: an otherwise idle pool still runs them. 0 or 1 lifts the cap. ASSIGNMENT_AGENT_MAX_SHARE No 0.5 The same share for one agent, inside or outside a fleet. 0 or 1 lifts the cap. DELEGATION_RESERVE_SLOTS No 2 Slots per worker above the shared pool that only a delegated child (an assignment child run or a background task) whose parent run is still running may take, once the pool is full: parents waiting on their own children never hold the pool until a deadline. 0 turns the reserve off. ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_BACKLOG_SECONDS No 300 Once an assignment's oldest queued delivery has waited this many seconds, the drain alternates its newest and oldest deliveries, so fresh work does not wait behind the whole backlog (nothing is dropped), and logs Assignment dispatch lag at WARNING at most once a minute. 0 disables both. ASSIGNMENT_DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF_SECONDS No 60 How long an assignment's concurrency cap stays halved after one of its runs met an HTTP 429, from a model provider or an integration. Only that assignment backs off; a 429 met anywhere else (a chat, an evaluation, an embedding) throttles nothing. The window starts at the first 429 and is not extended by the ones that follow. The providers' own retries are unchanged. 0 disables the back-off. ORCHESTRATION_MAX_QUEUE_WAIT_SECONDS No 3600 How long an assignment run or a background task may wait for a free worker before it fails with the cause deadline_exceeded_before_start (nothing runs, nothing is charged, no run.failed event). A run's timeout_seconds is its execution time and counts from the moment a worker starts it, never from its creation, so time spent in the queue is not taken from it. 0 removes the queue bound. An assignment's trigger_config.max_queue_wait_seconds overrides it. ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH No 20 Maximum deliveries held per assignment. Bounds the backlog a slow or stuck assignment can accumulate. ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_OVERFLOW_POLICY No reject Per-assignment webhook only: what happens to one of its deliveries arriving at a full queue (a queued integration event is never dropped). reject: HTTP 429 + Retry-After, so a sender with retry logic loses nothing. drop_oldest: the oldest waiting delivery is finalized as a skipped run (visible, payload preserved) and the new one takes its slot. drop_newest: the incoming delivery is discarded with a 200 and a warning — no run row is created. ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS No 30 Retry-After value returned with the reject policy's 429. ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_HOLD_ON_AWAITING_HUMAN No true Whether a run paused for human input holds the queue. true starts nothing more for its assignment until the approval is answered, whatever the cap - bounded and visible, unlike the old silent drop. false lets queued runs start beside a paused run; only safe when a HITL pause leaves no half-written shared state. ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_DRAIN_BATCH No 20 Maximum assignments that start queued runs per drain. Only assignments with a free slot are counted: one whose slots are all taken keeps its backlog without taking a turn. The drain runs on every reconciler cycle, on every enqueue and at the end of every run, so the rest follow within a cycle. WEBHOOK_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE No 60 Per-assignment delivery throttle, applied before the request body is read. Over-limit deliveries get 429 + Retry-After. Raise it for a high-cadence alert feed — the queue still bounds how many accepted deliveries become runs. WEBHOOK_EXACT_EVENT_MATCHING No false Event matching of integration-event and webhook triggers. A trigger created on this version, or whose events are chosen again, matches its event exactly: pull_request runs on pull_request.opened, never on pull_request_review.submitted. A trigger saved on an earlier version keeps its prefix match through every other edit and every copy (duplicate, import, catalog clone); its assignment page says which mode it uses and what it matches, with a one-click switch, and the first delivery it matches only by prefix is logged. true applies exact matching to every trigger without editing them; it does not read the old event_type key of an agent-builder trigger, which only that trigger's own switch does. Also in Settings > Access and security ("Exact event matching for every trigger"); the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. See Event matching. WEBHOOK_DEDUP_TTL_SECONDS No 300 Idempotency window. A delivery whose key was already seen within the window replays the first delivery's response instead of firing a second run. CHAT_EVENT_COALESCE_WINDOW_SECONDS No 6 One turn per chat conversation (a Teams 1:1 or group chat, a Teams channel thread, a Slack DM, channel or thread). The run of a message starts this many seconds late; a later message of the same sender in the same conversation that finds it still waiting joins its turn (one run, one reply, the messages in order and flagged as merged) instead of starting a second run. An assignment's trigger_config.coalesce_window_seconds overrides it (0-60); 0 turns the window off.

ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_ENABLED, ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_OVERFLOW_POLICY and ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS govern the per-assignment webhook (POST /api/hooks/assignments/{id}) only; the concurrency, depth, hold, backlog and back-off settings apply to every queued delivery.

A polled email, Teams or Slack message is always queued. Each poll reads its provider's events oldest first, up to 5 pages - 15 Microsoft emails, 10 Gmail messages, 20 Teams or Slack messages a page - and queues them, so a backlog drains as fast as the assignment's slots allow instead of one event per poll. When the queue is full, the rest is given back to the poller with its position and fetched again on a later tick; nothing is dropped. A backlog larger than one poll is logged once at INFO level. What a poll cannot fetch is logged as a warning: more than 250 new messages in one Teams channel or 1,000 in one Slack channel, more than 100 unread Gmail messages, more than a page of new Teams, Slack or Gmail events sharing one timestamp, or more than 1,000 Microsoft emails received within one second (a second holding more emails than a page is read whole before the poll moves past it). Events that arrived while the platform was down stay with their provider and are read the same way once it is back: the poll resumes from its saved position (kept 30 days) and skips events it already dispatched (kept 7 days).

A pushed event - a Slack event, a Microsoft Graph or LinkedIn notification, a provider or agent webhook - starts in a free slot. With every slot taken, it is skipped unless INTEGRATION_EVENT_QUEUE_ENABLED is true, in which case it is queued past the cap with a warning in the log.

An assignment's trigger configuration can refine the queue:

trigger_config key Effect max_concurrent_runs This assignment's cap, overriding ASSIGNMENT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS (1-50). 1 runs its deliveries one at a time. max_queue_wait_seconds How long one of its runs may wait for a free worker, overriding ORCHESTRATION_MAX_QUEUE_WAIT_SECONDS (0: no bound). Past it the run fails as deadline_exceeded_before_start, with trigger_context.queue.queue_wait_seconds recorded. ordering_key A dotted path into the trigger payload, such as issue.number. Runs whose payload has the same value there start one at a time, in arrival order; runs with different values, or none, run side by side. Mail triggers are ordered by thread without it (Microsoft conversation_id, Gmail thread_id), and chat messages by their conversation (conversation_key: a Teams chat, a Teams channel thread, a Slack DM or channel, a Slack thread); "" turns that off. coalesce_window_seconds The coalescing window of this assignment's chat messages, overriding CHAT_EVENT_COALESCE_WINDOW_SECONDS (0-60). batch_window_seconds integration_event and platform_event triggers only (0-600, default 0: one run per event). The first event opens a batch run that starts once the window ends; every event arriving while it waits joins it. The run's payload carries batch: true, event_count and events, the list in arrival order (at most 100 per batch, the next event opens a new one). Use it for observers of run.* events. preload_tool_groups Tool groups (ids such as integration:github, at most 6) every run of this assignment loads before its first request, so it never calls load_tools for them. A tool group loaded mid-run changes the tool list at the head of the request and invalidates the model provider's prompt cache for the rest of the run; a preloaded group keeps it valid. A group the agent does not hold is ignored. Any trigger type.

A chat message is never dropped for a busy assignment, whatever INTEGRATION_EVENT_QUEUE_ENABLED says: a message arriving while a run of its conversation is in flight is queued and starts when that run ends, so it is answered once, after the first reply. Messages of the same sender sent within the window are merged into one turn: the run's payload carries messages (in order), message_ids, the joined text, coalesced_count and a coalesced_note asking the agent to answer once.

A run that is not a delivery - a manual trigger, a follow-up, a scheduled or chained run - has its assignment to itself: deliveries wait until it ends, as they did before parallel runs. A delivery that cannot be queued (a pushed event with INTEGRATION_EVENT_QUEUE_ENABLED=false, the per-assignment webhook with ASSIGNMENT_QUEUE_ENABLED=false) never starts ahead of a queued run of its own ordering_key: it is skipped instead. One without a key may start in a free slot ahead of the queue.

The worker logs one line per drain (Assignment dispatch: promoted ...) and /metrics serves, per assignment (labelled by assignment_id, never by its name), xtmone_assignment_queue_depth, xtmone_assignment_queue_oldest_age_seconds, xtmone_assignment_runs_active, xtmone_assignment_concurrency_cap, xtmone_assignment_queue_held and xtmone_assignment_dispatch_lag_p95_seconds (created-to-started p95 over the last 15 minutes), plus xtmone_assignment_queue_oldest_age_max_seconds across assignments. k8s/prometheus-rules/assignment-dispatch-alerts.yaml alerts when a delivery has waited more than 5 minutes.

docs.title: Response statuses
docs.text: status Meaning ok A run started. triggered[0].run_id is its id. queued Accepted, waiting behind the active run. run_id is the queued run, queue_depth the current backlog. duplicate (with deduplicated: true) The same idempotency key already arrived within the window. The original response is replayed; nothing new was triggered. dropped The queue was full under drop_newest. This delivery will never run. ignored The target does not resolve (unknown, disabled, or not a webhook trigger), or an event filter excluded it. HTTP 429 Not accepted — retry after the Retry-After delay. Either the per-assignment throttle or a full queue under reject.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
